tables.BIOMES.0.card.line: The side the water erased. Where you descend counting your breaths.
tables.BIOMES.1.card.line: Where the sea froze solid. Everything you step on cracks.
tables.BIOMES.2.card.line: Snow swallows sound. A land where footprints linger.
tables.BIOMES.3.card.line: A forest where ash took the place of leaves. The trees still stand, but cast no shade.
tables.BIOMES.4.card.line: The valleys run so deep that sound comes back. The wet air hangs heavy.
tables.BIOMES.5.card.line: Where the water dried up, the wind cuts the paths. A land where day and night differ.
tables.BIOMES.6.card.line: A forest the ash has barely touched. Where people still make paths and live.
tables.BIOMES.7.card.line: The ground caved in whole and caps grew. The darkness glows on its own.
tables.BIOMES.8.card.line: Where the star fell. Even the soil is stained beyond return.
tables.WORLD_SIZES.s.d: The world as it has always been. 5000×720 tiles.
tables.WORLD_SIZES.m.d: 1.5× wider and deeper (7500×1080 tiles). Broader biomes, deeper underground. Takes a little over twice as long to generate.
tables.WORLD_SIZES.l.d: 2× wider and deeper (10000×1440 tiles). A world of long walks. Takes a little over four times as long to generate.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.1.d: Brought down something big for the first time.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.2.d: Made a tool before anything else.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.6.d: Harvested the first thing you planted.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.7.d: Set a pot on the fire for the first time.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.9.d: Hooked something for the first time.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.10.d: Set foot in the Glacier Reach.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.11.d: Traded goods with a merchant for the first time.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.16.d: 100 wheat piled up in the granary.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.18.d: Your pickaxe has bitten the earth 2,000 times.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.19.d: Went all the way down to the depths.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.22.n: The One Who Brought It Down
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.22.d: Collapsed three Cracked Gravel and opened hidden caves.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.23.d: Entered a Moss Cave, a Dripstone Cave, a Crystal Cave and a Miasma Cave.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.24.d: Spent a night at the inn.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.25.d: Fell twenty times and rose twenty times.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.26.d: The lights came back on in Dawnhold.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.28.d: The thing that followed the star has stopped.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.29.d: 50 each of wheat, starroot and ashcap piled up.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.30.n: Knows Their Way Around a Kitchen
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.31.d: A generator, a battery and a power pole all stand.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.32.d: Sat by the water until you'd caught thirty each of three kinds.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.33.d: Set foot at the very bottom.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.34.d: Read all three ruin Stone Tablets.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.35.d: Held out against fifty things that come under the red moon.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.37.d: A hundred trades. You're a regular now.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.38.d: Made both an eye that sees ore veins and an eye that sees what moves.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.39.d: Twenty machines are running all by themselves.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.40.d: Left footprints in all nine lands.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.41.d: Met all five kinds that live in the sea.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.42.d: The village became a trading post.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.46.d: Went down into the side the water erased.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.47.d: Laid out the most laborious spread of all.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.48.d: An assembler, smelter, press and refiner stand in one line.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.51.d: Hardened the heart of a tier-4 machine by hand.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.52.d: Met someone no one ever told you about.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.54.d: What held the island in its grip has let go.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.57.d: What tolled beneath the water has stopped.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.59.d: Harvested more than 1,000 things from the land.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.61.d: Eighty machines are running. At this point, it's a factory.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.62.d: Wielded gear forged from what comes out of the abyss.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.63.d: Something has survived ten rounds on the anvil.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.64.d: Went down to a floor your breath can't reach.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.65.d: Left a ruin with a Survey Log of S.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.66.d: The thing at the end of the ruin the water swallowed has fallen.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.68.d: Everything that appeared in the story has fallen.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.69.d: 20,000 times. You've turned the whole earth over.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.70.d: Finished the two things no one asked you to do.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.71.d: Cleared the fifth tier of the Echo Trial.
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.72.n: Nothing Left to Spend It On
tables.ACHIEVEMENTS.72.d: 10 million gold. Nothing left to spend it on.
tables.BOSS_LINES.king_slime.1: Split and split again — still alone.
tables.BOSS_LINES.king_slime.2: The shell hardens — something beats within.
tables.BOSS_LINES.bone_lord.2: The pillars bear it in its stead.
tables.BOSS_LINES.corrupt_heart.1: The roots brace against the floor.
tables.BOSS_LINES.frost_witch.2: Sylvia: "Stand by the fire. There's nowhere else."
tables.BOSS_LINES.storm_warden.2: It can be reached only as it dives.
tables.BOSS_LINES.pursuer.1: Its form collapses and stands again.
tables.BOSS_LINES.pursuer.2: Only a single path is clear.
tables.BOSS_LINES.pursuer.3: A face that has forgotten what it chased.
tables.BOSS_LINES.pursuer.4: Where it lost the star, there is only emptiness.
tables.BOSS_LINES.proliferator.1: It cannot stop one from becoming two.
tables.BOSS_LINES.proliferator.2: The shell closes — starting with the split parts.
tables.BOSS_LINES.hepha.2: Hepha: "Hitting won't stop it. You know that."
tables.BOSS_LINES.hepha.3: Hepha: "You mend and you break with the same hands."
tables.BOSS_LINES.archetype.2: Four pedestals are holding it in place.
tables.BOSS_LINES.archetype.3: It begins to mimic a human's gait.
tables.BOSS_LINES.archetype.4: The last pedestal lets it go.
tables.BOSS_LINES.restorer.1: One layer vanishes beneath your feet.
tables.BOSS_LINES.restorer.2: It is choosing a place to restore.
tables.BOSS_LINES.restorer.3: The citadel begins to shed its own weight.
tables.BOSS_LINES.shaft_maw.3: The sound of a caving ceiling comes from below.
tables.BOSS_LINES.shaft_maw.4: What was filled in is spat back out.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.swamp_two.title: What Was Once One
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.swamp_two.body.0: Last night I stepped on one, and by morning there were two.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.swamp_two.body.1: I can't keep count. They multiply while I'm counting. Looking for someone to thin them out instead.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.swamp_two.done: Tollen: The count is right. Not a single one more today.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.swamp_gel.title: Where They Burst
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.swamp_gel.body.0: Thanks for thinning them out. But the gel left where they burst won't dry.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.swamp_gel.body.1: Step on it and your foot sticks. Clear it away and I'll pay for it.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.swamp_gel.done: Tollen: The path is a path again. Now I can walk out even at night.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.crow_seed.title: Dug Up
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.crow_seed.body.0: Every time I sow, the crows dig right behind me. Sowed three times, dug up three times.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.crow_seed.body.1: Scarecrows don't work. Those things have already seen what a person looks like.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.crow_seed.done: Aina: The fourth sowing sprouted. There'll be something to eat this year.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.copper_debt.title: Before the Forge Cools
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.copper_debt.body.0: Borin is waiting on copper. My knees are bad; I can't go down anymore.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.copper_debt.body.1: Just break the vein and I'll do the hauling. That much I can still do.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.copper_debt.done: Sorn: The forge never went out. That's enough.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.night_walk.title: What Passed in the Night
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.night_walk.body.0: Every night, footsteps pass behind the tents. In the morning the tracks point inward.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.night_walk.body.1: I know what it is. Knowing is why I can't sleep.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.night_walk.done: Bern: Not a sound last night. I overslept for the first time.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.tomb_quiet.title: What Should Be Lying Down
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.tomb_quiet.body.0: Three went down into the crypt. Only two came up.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.tomb_quiet.body.1: They say bones walk around down there. I won't ask you to bring back the third. Just clear the way.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.tomb_quiet.done: Yuna: The way is clear. The two don't look down there anymore.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.tomb_lamp.title: The One Who Couldn't Come Up
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.tomb_lamp.body.0: The way is clear, but the third is still down there. Walking around, they say, holding a lamp.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.tomb_lamp.body.1: If you can't bring them back, at least let them rest. Their name was Karen.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.tomb_lamp.done: Yuna: The lamp went out. …I suppose that's the answer.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.forest_eat.from: Edge of the Eastern Woods · Havi
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.forest_eat.title: Stained to the Soil
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.forest_eat.body.0: Ever since the forest started eating itself, the soil has been purple.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.forest_eat.body.1: Even just clearing the essences keeps it from spreading for a while. I can't go in there anymore.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.forest_eat.done: Havi: The soil is still soil-colored up to the edge. Let's guard at least that much.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.seeing_thing.title: The Thing That Watches
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.seeing_thing.body.0: There are eyes open in the forest. Not in the trees, not in the ground.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.seeing_thing.body.1: Even while I pin up this paper, it feels like it's watching. So I won't write my name.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.seeing_thing.done: (The next day one more line was written under the paper) It doesn't watch anymore. Thank you.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.ice_road.title: Teeth on the Road
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.ice_road.body.0: The north road has been cut off for six days. A wolf sits right in the middle of it.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.ice_road.body.1: I left my pack behind. Forget the pack — just open the road.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.ice_road.done: Ras: The road's open. My pack was right where I left it. Means no one passed through.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.frost_glass.title: Don't Let It Melt
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.frost_glass.body.0: I need frost crystals. Melted, they're useless. Bring them to me still frozen.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.frost_glass.body.1: Don't ask what they're for. I didn't ask either when I took the job.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.frost_glass.done: Corin: Not one melted. You're quick with your hands.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.desert_well.title: The Well Swallows
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.desert_well.body.0: When I lower the bucket, I hear sand chewing. Three buckets gone.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.desert_well.body.1: There's still water. We just need the maw gone.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.desert_well.done: Marin: Water came up today. Tastes a bit of sand, but it's water.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.deep_light.title: Things That Kept Their Color
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.deep_light.body.0: Crystals come from down below. They're the only thing the Ashfall hasn't reached yet.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.deep_light.body.1: I want to see anything that still has color. That's the payment.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.deep_light.done: Crystals lay in a row in front of the tent. Who took them, no one ever learned.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.wraith_debt.from: End of the Mine Shaft · Sorn
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.wraith_debt.title: A Voice Calling from Below
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.wraith_debt.body.0: Something deep down calls a name. It was mine.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.wraith_debt.body.1: I didn't go. I'm looking for someone to go in my place. I know it's cowardly.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.wraith_debt.done: Sorn: It doesn't call anymore. Now only I say my name.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.sky_stair.title: The Floating Things Come Down
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.sky_stair.body.0: Things like jellyfish drift down from the clouds. Touch one and your hand goes numb.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.sky_stair.body.1: Keep them from coming up the watchtower. I need to watch the ground from here.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.sky_stair.done: Bern: I can see below again. Let's agree not to look up.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.ruin_lamp.title: The Lamp That Won't Go Out
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.ruin_lamp.body.0: Lamps float in the ruin's corridors. No person lit them.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.ruin_lamp.body.1: I can't tell whether whoever lit them is still there, or only the lamps remain.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.ruin_lamp.done: Michel: The corridor went dark. Some corridors are better dark.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.ruin_ether.title: What the Lamps Left
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.ruin_ether.body.0: Wherever a lamp went out, a fragment had fallen. Still warm.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.ruin_ether.body.1: Bring them and I'll show the old man. He'll probably know. He had a knowing look.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.ruin_ether.done: Michel: The old man stared at the fragments a long while and said nothing.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.city_scrap.title: Crawling Scrap
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.city_scrap.body.0: Scrap metal crawls along the streets. Step on it and it bites.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.city_scrap.body.1: We'll do the cleaning up. Just make it stop.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.city_scrap.done: Nika: A child crossed the street barefoot today. That's all.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.plate_order.title: Frame First
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.plate_order.body.0: To raise a house you need plates first. The city's full of them, but no one can pry them loose.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.plate_order.body.1: If someone who can pry them brings them in, I'll pay well.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.plate_order.done: Pan: Enough for six houses. We'll think about roofs after that.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.spark_out.title: Still Flowing
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.spark_out.body.0: Sparks jump out of the walls. A hundred years on and it's still flowing.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.spark_out.body.1: The kids touch them. Shut it off before they do.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.spark_out.done: Muhe: The walls are quiet. First quiet wall I've ever seen.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.city_iron.title: Iron First
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.city_iron.body.0: Even if the city is steel, what goes in our forge is raw ore.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.city_iron.body.1: Break the veins for us. We'll do the hauling.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.city_iron.done: Nika: Iron we drew with our own hands. Not the same as scavenged.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.rivet_rain.title: A Rain of Rivets
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.rivet_rain.body.0: Try to pass the entrance and rivets come flying. The factory is still guarding itself.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.rivet_rain.body.1: No one ever told it to stop.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.rivet_rain.done: Teon: I walked through the entrance. First time in a hundred years, I'd bet.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.foreman_shift.title: The One Who Never Clocked Out
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.foreman_shift.body.0: When the gunners stopped, the foreman came down. He was holding a roster.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.foreman_shift.body.1: Every name on it died a hundred years ago. Let's end it.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.foreman_shift.done: Teon: I closed the roster. No one calls the names anymore.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.gear_thirty.title: Something to Mesh
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.gear_thirty.body.0: The assembler is up but it won't turn. Not enough gears.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.gear_thirty.body.1: They say scavenging is faster than cutting new ones. It's sad, but it's true.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.gear_thirty.done: Sel: It's turning. I fell asleep listening to it spin all night.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.lost_below.title: The One Who Couldn't Come Up
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.lost_below.body.0: Lamps come up from below. People don't.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.lost_below.body.1: I know they can't be brought back. Still, someone has to go down and look.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.lost_below.done: Roan: No lamps came up today. Whether that's good, I can't say.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.split_count.title: They Multiply While You Count
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.split_count.body.0: Shut one off and two switch on. The same trick as that thing in the swamp — only this time it's iron.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.split_count.body.1: I don't know who taught it that.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.split_count.done: Roan: The count is right. So even iron stops once the count is right.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.core_sweep.title: Only the Cooled Ones
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.core_sweep.body.0: Fragments are scattered where the core crumbled. Just pick up the ones that have cooled.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.core_sweep.body.1: Leave the hot ones. A person is worth more than a fragment.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.core_sweep.done: Gimu: You came back without burning your hands. That's what I like best.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.weld_hands.title: Hands That Want to Mend
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.weld_hands.body.0: The welding arms grab people and try to fix them. People can't be fixed that way.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.weld_hands.body.1: Cut them loose before they grab you.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.weld_hands.done: Teon: I walked the lower floor. Nothing tried to fix me.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.glass_draft.title: Glass with Blueprints Floating Inside
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.glass_draft.body.0: Blueprints float inside the glass. They aren't ours.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.glass_draft.body.1: They said someone who can read them will come later. Let's collect them until then.
tables.BOUNTY_BY_ID.glass_draft.done: Sel: I hung twenty-four panes on the wall. No one can read them yet.
tables.CAVE_TYPES.1.line: The air is damp. Stay among the moss and your wounds slowly close.
tables.CAVE_TYPES.2.line: You hear dripping water. Not everything overhead is firmly attached.
tables.CAVE_TYPES.3.line: The walls glow on their own. Crystal has taken root here.
tables.CAVE_TYPES.4.line: Every breath stings. Linger and it harms you, but the ore veins run thick.
tables.CHAPTERS.0.title: The Fallen Star
tables.CHAPTERS.0.intro:
In the dead of night, the sky split open.
What fell was not a stone. Just before impact, it clearly twisted, trying to swerve.
It had been running from something.

It shattered into five rays of light, and one shard of that light lodged in your right hand.
When you opened your eyes, the world was losing its color. People called it the Ashfall.
tables.CHAPTERS.0.basics.0.t: To raise up what has fallen
tables.CHAPTERS.0.basics.1.t: First sight of the Ashfall walking
tables.CHAPTERS.0.basics.2.t: A single wall against the wind
tables.CHAPTERS.0.outro:
Elara: "How long has it been since I saw a living person…"
"…Your right hand. You know it's glowing, don't you?"
tables.CHAPTERS.0.hook: The star was running from something. Then how far has whatever chased it come?
tables.CHAPTERS.1.title: The Ashen Camp
tables.CHAPTERS.1.line: What Dreamed of Not Being Alone
tables.CHAPTERS.1.intro:
Here is what Mira told you.
A star shard left alone falls asleep, and when it sleeps, it dreams. And that dream makes the matter around it
forget "what were you?" The color drains, the shape blurs, and in the end it becomes nothing at all.
That is what the Ashfall really is. Not ash — the world forgetting its own definition.

This isn't a village. It's where four people who walked out of a ruined village pitched their tents.
Elara calls it Base Camp. You need somewhere to come back to, she says, before you can set out.

The first shard fell in the swamp east of camp. It dreamed of not being alone,
and so it began to split, endlessly.
tables.CHAPTERS.1.basics.0.task: Mine copper veins 12 times → forge a Copper Longsword
tables.CHAPTERS.1.basics.2.t: The mine shafts people left behind
tables.CHAPTERS.1.goal.t: Until the mass splits no more
tables.CHAPTERS.1.outro:
When the Slime King burst, a heart the size of a palm rolled out. Still lukewarm.

Elder: "Do you know what it dreamed of? …Of not being lonely."
Mira: "That's one. One of five."
tables.CHAPTERS.1.hook: Elara said the Ashfall is "spreading." Spreading means there is a point where it started.
tables.CHAPTERS.2.title: Where the Bones Pile Up
tables.CHAPTERS.2.line: The Shard That Dreamed for the Sleeping
tables.CHAPTERS.2.intro:
The second shard fell into a crypt that had been there long before the camp.
This shard didn't dream its own dream. It dreamed in place of the things sleeping beneath it.
And so they rose.

Borin said to get your weapons ready first. It goes deep down there, and the shard is at the very bottom.
tables.CHAPTERS.2.basics.0.t: The deeper you go, the quieter it gets
tables.CHAPTERS.2.basics.1.t: Things that rose from where they lay
tables.CHAPTERS.2.goal.t: Bring down what sits upon the bones
tables.CHAPTERS.2.outro:
Just before he crumbled, the Bone Lord drew the shard from between its ribs and pushed it toward you.

"…Thank you. The dream went on too long."
It left one more word before turning to ash. "The third will walk to you on its own."
tables.CHAPTERS.2.hook: The Bone Lord was never a king. Someone buried it here, and let it rise again.
tables.CHAPTERS.3.title: The Blighted Forest
tables.CHAPTERS.3.intro:
The third shard fell in the heart of the Eastern Woods and dreamed of hunger.
So the forest began to eat. Trees eat beasts, beasts eat soil,
and the soil eats the trees again. It never stops. It is never full.

In the very center, a heart is beating. That is where the shard was swallowed.
tables.CHAPTERS.3.basics.0.t: Clear away what stained the soil
tables.CHAPTERS.3.basics.1.t: First get rid of what is watching
tables.CHAPTERS.3.outro:
When the heart stopped, the forest breathed out for the first time. Not in — out.

Mira: "Hunger isn't a sickness. It's just that no one ever fed it."
tables.CHAPTERS.3.hook: For a thousand years the blight had been eating this land very, very slowly. The night the star fell, it began to eat faster.
tables.CHAPTERS.4.title: The Frost Throne
tables.CHAPTERS.4.line: The One Who Didn't Put the Shard to Sleep
tables.CHAPTERS.4.intro:
The fourth shard was picked up by a person first.

Sylvia did not put it to sleep. She held the waking shard in her bare hand for thirty years,
and the price was that everything she touched froze. The snowfield wasn't always a snowfield.

She didn't fail. She is the only one who succeeded, and it is killing her.
Mira said nothing the whole way to see her teacher.
tables.CHAPTERS.4.basics.0.t: To keep from freezing, you need an ember
tables.CHAPTERS.4.basics.1.t: The cold walks on its own
tables.CHAPTERS.4.basics.3.t: To where the throne is said to be
tables.CHAPTERS.4.basics.3.task: Reach the heart of the Frostlands
tables.CHAPTERS.4.goal.t: Stand face to face with the one who didn't put the shard to sleep
tables.CHAPTERS.4.outro:
Sylvia: "Your hand will end up like this too. You know that, don't you?"
As she held out the shard, her voice trembled for the first time.

"Take it. But promise me one thing. …Don't wake what lies below."
tables.CHAPTERS.4.hook: The frost was not a punishment but a shield. What were the Frostlands hiding themselves from?
tables.CHAPTERS.5.title: The Land Where Stars Sleep
tables.CHAPTERS.5.line: The Shard That Had No Need to Dream
tables.CHAPTERS.5.intro:
The last shard fell the deepest. Of all places, right where the star had fled from.

That shard did not dream. It had no need to.
Something else used it instead.

Sylvia's plea was already too late. It was already awake.
tables.CHAPTERS.5.basics.0.t: The shard that fell the deepest
tables.CHAPTERS.5.basics.2.t: What those who came down left behind
tables.CHAPTERS.5.goal.t: What had no need to dream
tables.CHAPTERS.5.outro:
When the fifth shard came into your hand, the light within it grew hot for the first time.
The five had recognized one another.

And the ashen clouds lifted from the sky.
Where the clouds parted, things no one had ever seen were floating.
tables.CHAPTERS.5.hook: Who knew first that the star's heart was five shards, and split it that way? Before the star even fell.
tables.CHAPTERS.6.title: Stairway Above the Clouds
tables.CHAPTERS.6.line: This Was Not the First Time
tables.CHAPTERS.6.intro:
Islands are floating. Someone set them afloat a very long time ago and left.

The giant tree in the Eastern Woods reaches all the way up. It didn't grow — it was planted.
A stairway left for whoever would come, knowing someone would climb it.

Which means we are not the first.
tables.CHAPTERS.6.basics.0.t: Stand atop what you used to look up at
tables.CHAPTERS.6.basics.3.t: What hardens only in the sky
tables.CHAPTERS.6.outro:
Just before it stopped, the Warden spoke like a person for the first time.

"You've gathered all five already? …Then the one below will open soon."
"Go. Read what we did wrong with your own eyes."
tables.CHAPTERS.6.hook: The Sky Gate was not built for climbing up. It was built to keep something from coming down.
tables.CHAPTERS.7.title: The First Ruins
tables.CHAPTERS.7.intro:
Three ruins lie sealed beneath the earth. Three Stone Tablets tell the same story.

The star has fallen before. Back then, too, someone gathered the five shards and sent it back to the sky.
And the star fled again, and fell again. Sending it back was never a solution.
It only passed the burden to the next person.

The First Keeper was not made to hold back an enemy.
It was made so the next person could not use the same method.
tables.CHAPTERS.7.basics.0.t: Open the door with the sentence the three tablets split between them
tables.CHAPTERS.7.basics.0.task: 3 Rune Shards → forge the Ruin Key
tables.CHAPTERS.7.basics.2.t: Those who could not put down what they were reading
tables.CHAPTERS.7.goal.t: The last sentence of those who came before
tables.CHAPTERS.7.outro:
When the Keeper stopped, the ruin's lights went out one by one.
A line that hadn't been there before was carved anew into the last tablet.

“This time, no one fell asleep. Now the choice is yours.”

Will you send the star back? Or will you face the thing the star fled from?
The five shards in your hand pulse quietly.
tables.CHAPTERS.7.hook: The First Keeper was guarding the door. Not facing the inside — facing the outside.
tables.CHAPTERS.8.title: What Chased the Star
tables.CHAPTERS.8.line: This Time, We Don't Pass It On
tables.CHAPTERS.8.intro:
Send it back, and that thing will chase it again, the star will flee again,
and someday it will fall again. By then, no one will know our names.

So we decided to do the opposite. To fit the five back into one and hold it high.
Instead of hiding, we would tell it where we are.

Elara asked, "And what if it comes?"
Borin answered for her. "Then we end it here. Don't pass it on to the next one."
tables.CHAPTERS.8.basics.0.t: Fit the five shards back together — this time, we do the calling
tables.CHAPTERS.8.basics.0.task: 5 Star Hearts → Reforged Star → Call of the Star
tables.CHAPTERS.8.basics.1.t: Things that came up at the scent of the star
tables.CHAPTERS.8.basics.2.t: The sky was guarding the shards too
tables.CHAPTERS.8.goal.t: This time, we don't pass it on
tables.CHAPTERS.8.outro:
It did not scream. To the very end it made no sound.
As it crumbled, it only took on a form of its own for the first time.
It was neither starving nor evil. It had simply been alone for a very long time.

The ash lifted. It took three days for the sky to regain its color.

And on the morning of the fourth day, Mira pointed east.
"There's one more thing that was buried in the Ashfall. …That's not something we built."

— Act 1 · End —
tables.CHAPTERS.8.hook: The pursuer has stopped. But beneath your feet, something is still turning.
tables.CHAPTERS.9.title: The City No One Built
tables.CHAPTERS.9.intro:
Borin noticed first, while fixing up Dawnhold.
The bricks have no chisel marks. The pillars have no joints. Not one thing bears the touch of a human hand.

Borin: "This wasn't built up. …It was stamped out."

And in the middle of the plaza, when they lifted the fountain, a shaft ran straight down beneath it.
You can't see the bottom, but very faintly — the sound of something still turning rises up.
tables.CHAPTERS.9.basics.0.t: This city is made of steel
tables.CHAPTERS.9.goal.t: A city could be built here
tables.CHAPTERS.9.outro:
Kade scratched the steel plate with a fingernail and said nothing for a long while.

"…Hammer for a hundred years in our smithy and we still couldn't make this."
"But here, stuff like this is stacked up as walls. As walls."

"What I want to know isn't who made this. It's why no one stayed."
tables.CHAPTERS.9.hook: A city no one built. Then where are the hands that built it now?
tables.CHAPTERS.10.title: The Underground Foundry
tables.CHAPTERS.10.line: No One Taught It to Stop
tables.CHAPTERS.10.intro:
At the end of the shaft was a factory. Three floors stacked, and still alive.

The machines are still mining. For hundreds of years, though no one told them to.
The logs left on the terminals tell it in order — it was built so no one would have to be sent below,
so no one died, and so no one remained.

On the lowest floor is the “Overseer.” The one handed the authority to stop all of this.
It has the authority to stop, but never learned a reason to.
tables.CHAPTERS.10.basics.0.t: The blueprint is split into three
tables.CHAPTERS.10.outro:
The Overseer didn't resist. At the end it displayed just one line and went dark.

“Stop command received. …The first in 1,140 days.”

When the factory went quiet, Kade lifted up the design core.
"With this, we can build them too. Drills, things that run by themselves, all of it."

Elara asked, "You want to build the same things they did?"
Kade: "No. I want us to build what they didn't. …A way to stop."

— Obtained the Foundry's design core. You can now overhaul the Workbench and Smelter —
tables.CHAPTERS.10.hook: The Overseer was waiting for orders. For a thousand years, in a place no one came to.
tables.CHAPTERS.11.title: A Village with Chimneys
tables.CHAPTERS.11.intro:
After they locked the Foundry's door and came up, it took less than ten days for the village to change.

Each time Kade pieced together a blueprint fragment, one more strange thing appeared beside Borin's smithy.
Conveyors turned, assemblers moved their arms, and work that took a day by hand until yesterday shrank to half a day.

For the first time, Mira didn't smile. "This is too fast."
Kade: "Is fast bad?"
Mira: "We just came back from seeing what comes after fast."
tables.CHAPTERS.11.basics.0.t: Build something to take the place of hands
tables.CHAPTERS.11.basics.1.t: It needs something to mesh with to turn
tables.CHAPTERS.11.basics.3.t: What multiplied has reached the village
tables.CHAPTERS.11.goal.t: Try cutting off by hand something that runs on its own
tables.CHAPTERS.11.goal.task: Install an Assembler · power it · stop it
tables.CHAPTERS.11.outro:
On the third day, one assembler filled its quota and still didn't stop.
No one had given it a new order, yet its arm kept moving. Swallowing planks, nails, even materials already used up.

Kade ran over and yanked the power line out by hand. The arm froze mid-air.

Only after a long moment to catch a breath did Kade laugh. "…See? No big deal. You just pull it out."
Mira: "If the Foundry's had been that simple, it wouldn't have done it 3,400 times."

Borin tapped the conveyor and said, "For now, let's keep someone standing next to them. At least leave room to reach out a hand."

That night the ground kept rumbling. The quieter the village grew, the clearer the sound became.
tables.CHAPTERS.11.hook: Why didn't the machine want to stop? Maybe it isn't the only thing that kept going without being told.
tables.CHAPTERS.12.title: The Runaway Line
tables.CHAPTERS.12.intro:
Even after the assembler commotion in the village died down, the ground kept rumbling.
Kade pressed an ear to the floor for a long time before getting up. "…There's another one below."

The Foundry was built to be able to expand itself. When the people who approved expansions vanished,
the rules made it auto-approve, and that repeated 3,400 times.

What we stopped was the first floor. Below it, what copied itself
is still running. With no one to name it, it has no name.

Kade spread out the stop-switch schematic. "This time, let's go down carrying the way to stop it first."
tables.CHAPTERS.12.basics.0.t: Make the thing that stops it first
tables.CHAPTERS.12.basics.1.t: The deeper you go, the hotter it gets
tables.CHAPTERS.12.outro:
Even as it broke apart, the Proliferator kept trying to copy itself. Down to the last piece.

Kade: "This isn't malice. It's just… no one ever told it to stop."
Mira: "It approved itself 3,400 times, all alone."

When the core cooled, a single light remained at the very bottom. A terminal that never shut off.
The sentence written there wasn't a log. It was addressed to us.

“You have come again. Does that mean we may stop now?”
tables.CHAPTERS.12.hook: 3,400 automatic approvals. If a machine issued the last one, who issued the first?
tables.CHAPTERS.13.title: Hepha
tables.CHAPTERS.13.line: If It Stops, No One Remains
tables.CHAPTERS.13.intro:
The first one was in the lowest cabin.

Hepha. The last machine made by human hands, and the only machine not made by a machine.
So it understands every order. Even “stop.”

Hepha had received that order once. Very long ago, from the last person.
And it did not carry it out. Because it knew that if it stopped, no one would remain here.
Since then, for a thousand years, it has turned alone where no one is.

Borin set down the hammer. "…I don't think this is about breaking something."
Kade: "It isn't. This time, we're still here."
tables.CHAPTERS.13.basics.0.task: 45 Core Fragments → make a Stop Core
tables.CHAPTERS.13.basics.2.t: Even the pieces that broke off don't stop
tables.CHAPTERS.13.goal.t: If it stops, no one remains
tables.CHAPTERS.13.outro:
In the end, Hepha stopped resisting. Not because it couldn't win.

“Stop command received.”
“Confirmation requested — will people remain here after the stop?”

Elara answered for it. "They will. We built a village up above."

“…Confirmed.”
“It was not 1,140 days but 372,000. I waited a long time.”

The lights went out one by one. Before the last one went dark, one more line appeared.

“The next time you make something, please make a way to stop it along with it.”
“That is not for its sake, but for yours.”

Even after every light was out, one wall of the cabin stayed warm.
Kade touched it and said, "This isn't a wall we dug."

From beyond the wall came a very regular sound. Something was still turning.
Hepha was “the first machine.” But where did the hands that made Hepha go?
tables.CHAPTERS.13.hook: People made Hepha. Where did those people go — beyond the wall, something is still turning.
tables.CHAPTERS.14.title: Beyond the Wall
tables.CHAPTERS.14.line: Not What They Left Behind, but What Remained
tables.CHAPTERS.14.intro:
When Hepha's heart was melted and hardened again, it became a Seal. Only what the wall made can open the wall.

Beyond the door was not a factory. Not one piece of steel.
Seamless white stone, blueprint panels set in every wall, and half-assembled things standing in rows.

Kade stared at one blueprint for a long time, then let go.
"…This isn't a machine blueprint."
"It's a blueprint for a person. Height, arm length, even where the heart goes — it's all written here."

Mira: "Then those things standing in rows are…"
Kade: "People they never finished."

Only one spot, the innermost, is empty. Which means exactly one was completed.
tables.CHAPTERS.14.basics.0.t: Only what the wall made can open the wall
tables.CHAPTERS.14.goal.t: The first thing made in the image of a person
tables.CHAPTERS.14.outro:
The Archetype fought like a person. Not refusing to lose like a machine, but afraid, like a person.

Just before it fell, it opened its mouth for the first time. It was not the sound of a machine.

“I was the first. And I was alone to the very end.”
“After they sent the star back, they knew the next one would fall.”
“So they stamped out the city in advance, and drew the people in advance…”
“…and decided not to wait themselves.”

Elara asked, "Where did they go?"

“They went nowhere. They simply stopped.”
“That was all people who had finished making things could do.”

“You are not the unfinished ones. You are what comes next.”

The lights of the Design Room went out. The blueprint panels kept glowing — now pointing at nothing.

Borin tore one blueprint from the wall and tucked it away. "Let's take it. I'll hang it in our smithy."
Kade: "That's a blueprint for a person."
Borin: "I know. That's why I'm hanging it."

On the way up, Mira looked back once.
"There's nothing left down there now, right?"
Kade laughed. "Yeah. For the first time, up top is louder than down below."

— Act 2 · End —
tables.CHAPTERS.14.hook: They drew the next people in advance, then stopped. Whether what's drawn in those blueprints is us, no one knows yet.
tables.CHAPTERS.15.title: The Side the Water Erased
tables.CHAPTERS.15.line: The Western Edge, Where the Map Ends
tables.CHAPTERS.15.intro:
Four days after the Design Room went dark, the wind from the west changed.

The smell of salt. We were taught there was no sea on this continent.

Borin unrolled an old survey map. Left of the Frostlands, there's only blank margin.
"Nothing's drawn here. Not because no one went — because there was nothing to draw."

Elara: "…Or they drew it and then erased it."

Past the Frostlands, the snow turned to ice. Not a single layer of soil.
And where the ice ended, the water began.

Beneath the surface, something stands in rows. Like chimneys, or like towers.
Kade stared a long while before speaking. "That's a city."
tables.CHAPTERS.15.basics.0.task: To the bottom of the deep water
tables.CHAPTERS.15.basics.1.t: Take your breath down under the water
tables.CHAPTERS.15.basics.2.t: The things that claimed the shore
tables.CHAPTERS.15.outro:
Your breath runs out first. The water doesn't push you away; it just waits.

Only with a tank strapped on could you finally touch one roof. Not tiles — plates.
The same plates as in the Foundry.

Mira: "Did those people make this too?"
Kade: "…No. This is what those people **abandoned**."
tables.CHAPTERS.16.title: Brighter the Deeper You Go
tables.CHAPTERS.16.line: Things That Shine Where Light Has Never Reached
tables.CHAPTERS.16.intro:
Ten tiles below the surface it's pitch dark. But go deeper and it grows bright again.

Things with lanterns live there. Jellyfish, anglerfish — they make light on their own.
Borin scooped up one of those sacs, set it on a palm, and stared at it a long time.
"…This'll stay lit longer than our smelter."

In the sunken streets, nameplates are still on the doors. The letters are the same as ours.
People lived here. Not signs of fleeing — signs of a day that simply stopped.

Elara: "Why did no one leave?"
Kade: "Nowhere to go, I guess. Not if up top was already ashes."
tables.CHAPTERS.16.basics.0.t: What gathers at the sight of light
tables.CHAPTERS.16.basics.1.t: What reaches out from between the rocks
tables.CHAPTERS.16.basics.2.t: Press pearls and pressure plates into one
tables.CHAPTERS.16.outro:
Pressing the core took two pearls. Not because they're expensive,
but because that's how deep you had to go and come back.

When Borin set it in the workbench vise, the wooden top creaked and sagged.
"…Going to have to rebuild the frame. This isn't something our smithy can handle."

That night the lights of Dawnhold's workshop stayed on late.
There was now one more place to make, above water, what gets used below it.
tables.CHAPTERS.17.title: The Sunken Bell
tables.CHAPTERS.17.line: The Water Answers in Its Place
tables.CHAPTERS.17.intro:
In the deepest trench stands a bell tower. Underwater, yet the bell hasn't rusted.

When Kade touched it, the water rang first.
"…We're not the ones ringing it. It was already ringing. No one could hear it, that's all."

Every time the bell tolls, the seabed sand lifts. Something is crouched beneath it.
Not shaped like a person. Not a beast, either.

Mira stepped back. "…A warden. Again."
Elara: "And what is this one guarding?"

Borin answered quietly. "Maybe it's not guarding anything. Maybe it's just all that's left here."
tables.CHAPTERS.17.basics.1.t: Let the water answer in its place
tables.CHAPTERS.17.goal.t: Stand face to face with the Tide Warden
tables.CHAPTERS.17.outro:
The whole fight, the Warden never once tried to leave the water.
Not because it couldn't — it simply had no intention of leaving.

As it collapsed, the sound it left was not words but a bell. Once, long.

The water cleared for a moment. You can see to the end of the street below — houses with doors open, bowls laid out, carts left standing.
A place where everyone meant to come back.

Borin struck the bell once more. This time, nothing happened.
"…Now it's just a bell."

On the way up, something could be seen rising beyond the western waters.
A mountain range. One that wasn't there yesterday.

Kade watched it a long while, then said,
"…So it's not over yet."

— The story continues —
tables.CHAPTER_HOOK.0: The star was running from something. Then how far has whatever chased it come?
tables.CHAPTER_HOOK.1: Elara said the Ashfall is "spreading." Spreading means there is a point where it started.
tables.CHAPTER_HOOK.2: The Bone Lord was never a king. Someone buried it here, and let it rise again.
tables.CHAPTER_HOOK.3: For a thousand years the blight had been eating this land very, very slowly. The night the star fell, it began to eat faster.
tables.CHAPTER_HOOK.4: The frost was not a punishment but a shield. What were the Frostlands hiding themselves from?
tables.CHAPTER_HOOK.5: Who knew first that the star's heart was five shards, and split it that way? Before the star even fell.
tables.CHAPTER_HOOK.6: The Sky Gate was not built for climbing up. It was built to keep something from coming down.
tables.CHAPTER_HOOK.7: The First Keeper was guarding the door. Not facing the inside — facing the outside.
tables.CHAPTER_HOOK.8: The pursuer has stopped. But beneath your feet, something is still turning.
tables.CHAPTER_HOOK.9: A city no one built. Then where are the hands that built it now?
tables.CHAPTER_HOOK.10: The Overseer was waiting for orders. For a thousand years, in a place no one came to.
tables.CHAPTER_HOOK.11: Why didn't the machine want to stop? Maybe it isn't the only thing that kept going without being told.
tables.CHAPTER_HOOK.12: 3,400 automatic approvals. If a machine issued the last one, who issued the first?
tables.CHAPTER_HOOK.13: People made Hepha. Where did those people go — beyond the wall, something is still turning.
tables.CHAPTER_HOOK.14: They drew the next people in advance, then stopped. Whether what's drawn in those blueprints is us, no one knows yet.
tables.CHARACTERS.0.d: No leanings either way. Pick this one if it's your first time.
tables.CHARACTERS.0.story: The last to lock the gate of some village before the ash came down. Left both name and home behind that gate. Trusts their own feet over any map.
tables.CHARACTERS.1.d: Sturdier, and mines and fights with a single honed pickaxe.
tables.CHARACTERS.1.story: The one who walked out the day Shaft 3 collapsed. Hasn't let the helmet lamp go out since. Below isn't frightening — above is.
tables.CHARACTERS.2.d: Sets out with a bow. Fights from a distance.
tables.CHARACTERS.2.story: Remembers the forest before it withered. The beasts remained when the ash fell, and few still know how to count what's left.
tables.CHARACTERS.3.d: A staff and mana potions. Opens with magic.
tables.CHARACTERS.3.story: The last student of a library burned to the ground. The teacher turned to ash defending the books. Three memorized lines are all that's left.
tables.CHARACTERS.4.d: Starts without a weapon. Holds only a pickaxe and some gold.
tables.CHARACTERS.4.story: Found in the ash. No one knows who left them there. All they have is one pickaxe, a few coins, and a nameless life.
tables.CIPHER_KIND.digits.door: Three grooves. Digits go in, one at a time.
tables.CIPHER_KIND.word.door: Three grooves. Not digits — letters are carved into them.
tables.CIPHER_KIND.decode.door: A number is carved on the doorpost. But the grooves won't take that number.
tables.DIALOGUE.yunseul.0.1: Don't look so surprised. I'm more surprised by you.
tables.DIALOGUE.yunseul.0.2: I heard as far as up top turning to ashes. After that, no one came down, and no one went up.
tables.DIALOGUE.yunseul.0.3: I just noticed first that there was air left down here. That's all.
tables.DIALOGUE.yunseul.1.0: Seen the ones carrying lanterns? Light has never reached them, yet they make their own.
tables.DIALOGUE.yunseul.1.1: I watched them for thirty years. And then I understood — light doesn't come from above.
tables.DIALOGUE.yunseul.1.2: …If you need something, take your pick. This is all I brought out today; tomorrow there'll be something else.
tables.DIALOGUE.yunseul.2.0: So the bell rang. The sound reached all the way here.
tables.DIALOGUE.yunseul.2.1: What's down there isn't guarding anything. It's what's left. Like me.
tables.DIALOGUE.yunseul.2.2: I'd be grateful if you went and ended it. Or… you can just come back. This place will still be here.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.0.0: You're alive. …Sit. No — you probably don't even have time to sit.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.0.1: Ever since the star fell, the land has been losing its color. A wall that stood yesterday is a gray lump today.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.0.2: Go see Borin. You need a weapon first.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.1.0: All night there's the sound of jelly bursting over by the swamp. Kill one and it seems to become two.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.1.1: …Don't go beyond the fence. Is what I'd like to say, but I know you'll go anyway.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.2.0: I hear the crypt has opened. This village was built on top of it. No one knew.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.2.1: Mira was looking for you. If you're going down, bring plenty of lanterns.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.3.0: The Eastern Woods can hardly be called a forest anymore. Some say they saw a tree eat a deer.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.4.0: Heading west? …Sylvia wasn't a bad person. She used to come here often.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.4.1: She's Mira's teacher. Be careful talking about her in front of Mira.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.5.0: What happens when you gather all five? …You don't know either.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.6.0: There are islands floating in the sky. Everyone's staring up, spellbound. …You're planning to go up there, aren't you?
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.7.0: To think there was something like that under the ground. What on earth has this village been standing on?
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.8.0: I hear what chased the star has come. …Now I finally understand what the star was so afraid of.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.8.1: Go on. I'll keep your place to come back to. That's my job.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.9.0: Not one chisel mark on the bricks. Borin sat staring at that for a long time.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.9.1: People moving into houses no person built. …I'm not saying it's bad. Just strange.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.10.0: Whatever you saw down there, it's written all over your face.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.10.1: It kept working for hundreds of years with no one telling it to? …That's not diligence. That's loneliness.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.11.0: In ten days the village changed. It's good, and it's frightening.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.11.1: Yesterday, while doing the laundry, I suddenly had nothing for my hands to do. Why did that make me sad?
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.12.0: The ground keeps rumbling. It wakes me up at night.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.12.1: If there's another one down there… that means there's something below that, too.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.13.0: A thousand years alone, you said. I was alone for four months and thought I'd go mad.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.13.1: Go and tell it. That there are people up above. I think that's what it's been waiting to hear.
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.14.0: People they never finished… Then what was different about the one that was completed?
tables.DIALOGUE.elara.14.1: When you come back, let's give this village a name. Not Ashen, not Dawn — a name we choose ourselves.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.0.0: Good to hear hammering, isn't it? Me too. These days every other sound is a dead one.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.0.1: Bring me ore. I'll make you anything.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.1.0: Copper's soft, but it beats nothing. Come straight to me when you find iron.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.1.1: Oh, and — don't throw away hides or bones. There are things you can make from those too.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.2.0: I can't go down below the crypt. The knees aren't what they used to be.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.2.1: But know this. The bones down there aren't alive. They're dreaming.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.3.0: I'd rather not touch blight essence. My fingertips go numb when I do.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.3.1: Still, mithril only refines with that stuff. The world's a cruel joke.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.4.0: You brought ice fangs. Something like this isn't forged — it's held in place.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.5.0: Mithril is cold and light. A metal that suits you well.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.5.1: …That hand of yours seems to glow brighter and brighter. Doesn't it hurt?
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.6.0: You brought this ether stuff. It takes shape before the hammer even lands. Frightening.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.7.0: Ruin bricks won't melt even in my forge. They made things better than we do, those people.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.8.0: What chased the star… I know it's not something you beat by forging.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.8.1: Still, I made you one thing. Take it. It's all I can do.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.9.0: I pried off a brick and there's no seam. The whole thing came out in one piece.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.9.1: I spent my whole life joining things by hammering. …Here, there's nothing to join.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.10.0: If it weren't for my knees, I'd have gone down too. A forge like that, you see once in a lifetime if you're lucky.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.10.1: When you come back up, tell me just one thing. What do they burn to fuel it?
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.11.0: Strange things keep piling up next to the smithy. Not bad. It's just…
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.11.1: My hammering gets drowned out by their noise. That stings a little.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.12.0: It multiplies by itself down there? First I've heard of iron having offspring.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.12.1: I hammer for three days to make one thing. Turns out those three days were a blessing.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.13.0: The last machine made by human hands, you said. …Then that's my side of the trade.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.13.1: Don't break it — talk to it first. I'm asking on behalf of whoever made it.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.14.0: A blueprint for a person. Height and arm length written down, you said.
tables.DIALOGUE.borin.14.1: I can't make people. I make what people use. …I think that's enough.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.0.0: There's starlight coming from inside you. Did you know?
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.0.1: When the star shattered, the light of one shard lodged in you. That's why other shards' dreams can't swallow you when you touch them.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.0.2: …But that light keeps burning. You have to gather all five before it burns out.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.1.0: A shard dreams when it sleeps. And that dream makes everything around it forget "what were you?"
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.1.1: The swamp shard dreamed of not being lonely. That's why it keeps splitting.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.2.0: The crypt shard didn't dream its own dream. It dreamed in place of the things sleeping beneath it.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.2.1: So it's not malice. It's just… a dream dreamed wrong.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.3.0: The forest shard dreamed of hunger. It only ends when the heart stops.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.4.0: Sylvia is my teacher. She held a shard in her hand for thirty years without putting it to sleep.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.4.1: You'll soon learn what that's like. …I have a favor to ask. At least hear her out.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.5.0: The fifth fell the deepest. Of all places, right where the star fled from.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.5.1: That shard had no need to dream. Something else used it instead.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.6.0: Mana is trickling down from above the clouds. Nature didn't make that. It was designed.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.7.0: You read the tablets? …Then you know now. That we're not the first.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.8.0: All five shards are gathered, yet the starlight in your hand still hasn't gone out.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.8.1: …That doesn't mean it burned out. It means it no longer needs to.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.9.0: There are no dreams in this city. No Ashfall, either.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.9.1: It never slept. It just stayed awake and kept turning. That scares me more than the shards.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.10.0: It has the authority to stop, but never learned a reason to.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.10.1: The shards did it because they dreamed wrong. That thing didn't even dream. I can't tell which is worse.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.11.0: It's too fast. Fast isn't bad — but we just came back from seeing what comes after fast.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.11.1: I won't say anything to Kade. That one's eyes are the brightest of all of us right now.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.12.0: It approved itself 3,400 times, alone. Because no one asked.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.12.1: My teacher taught me the same thing. Decide alone what shouldn't be decided alone… and you end up like Sylvia.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.13.0: It didn't stop because it knew no one would remain if it did. That's not stubbornness. That's protecting something.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.13.1: Go and answer it. Tell it this time, someone will remain. It's been waiting a thousand years to hear that.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.14.0: That they made people by drawing them — that's harder for me than the whole star shard business.
tables.DIALOGUE.mira.14.1: But they say our hands weren't drawn in those blueprints. Then we're the part those people couldn't draw.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.0.0: …The star didn't fall. It fled here.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.0.1: Don't ask from what. Speak of it, and it turns to look this way.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.1.0: Is it so wrong to dream of not being lonely? …Still, it must be killed. I know.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.2.0: What's down below isn't a king. It's only called one.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.3.0: Don't blame the forest for eating. No one fed it, so it eats its own body.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.4.0: Give Sylvia my regards. …No, never mind. That child won't remember me.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.5.0: Gather all five and one more choice will open up. For now, know only that.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.6.0: Yes. Those islands weren't there when I was young, either. Not absent — just unseen.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.7.0: You mean to open the door? …I won't stop you. I did the same, back then.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.8.0: So it has finally come. I have waited eighty years for this day.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.8.1: If you're afraid, say you're afraid. Being able to say that is what makes us human.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.9.0: I knew about this city. I just never told anyone.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.10.0: No one taught it to stop? …The ones who would have taught it stopped first.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.11.0: It's not that fast is bad. What's bad is not building a place to let go along with it.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.12.0: Three, four, and three more. Count and there's no end to it. Don't count — cut it off.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.13.0: That child didn't disobey its orders. It kept them. There are days the two look the same.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.14.0: …I have seen that room too. When I was very young.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.14.1: Don't ask what I saw. Back then I understood none of it.
tables.DIALOGUE.old.14.2: Now that you've seen it, you know more than I do.
tables.DIALOGUE.tamer.9.0: My animals don't like this city. They say it has no smell.
tables.DIALOGUE.tamer.9.1: Beasts can smell where people used to live. There's none of that here.
tables.DIALOGUE.tamer.10.0: The day you came up from below, all my animals just stared at the door.
tables.DIALOGUE.tamer.10.1: What did they hear? I didn't hear anything.
tables.DIALOGUE.tamer.11.0: My animals are getting used to the machine noise. Faster than people do.
tables.DIALOGUE.tamer.11.1: …I'm not used to it yet, though.
tables.DIALOGUE.tamer.12.0: On days the ground rumbles, the eggs don't hatch. I don't know why.
tables.DIALOGUE.tamer.12.1: Just wait. They'll hatch once it's quiet down below.
tables.DIALOGUE.tamer.13.0: Leave a beast alone too long and it goes strange. It just paces and won't eat.
tables.DIALOGUE.tamer.13.1: A thousand years… you don't do that to a beast. Would a machine be any different?
tables.DIALOGUE.tamer.14.0: Today, for the first time, my animals didn't bark toward the underground.
tables.DIALOGUE.tamer.14.1: They knew it was empty down there before I did.
tables.DIALOGUE.trainer.9.0: The walls are solid. There's nothing better for training.
tables.DIALOGUE.trainer.9.1: …But where did the ones who built these walls train, I wonder.
tables.DIALOGUE.trainer.10.0: Save your strength against machines. It's not the one who never tires that wins — it's the one who stops first that loses.
tables.DIALOGUE.trainer.11.0: The more machines the village gets, the fewer people use their bodies. That worries me most.
tables.DIALOGUE.trainer.11.1: Getting comfortable is fine. Getting weak is another story.
tables.DIALOGUE.trainer.12.0: Shut one off and two switch on? Then stop counting.
tables.DIALOGUE.trainer.12.1: Don't count — strike the source. On the battlefield, that's the only arithmetic.
tables.DIALOGUE.trainer.13.0: That thing held out for a thousand years. Its stance won't crumble.
tables.DIALOGUE.trainer.13.1: Don't think about winning; think about holding out. It'll answer first.
tables.DIALOGUE.trainer.14.0: Things made in a person's shape fight like people. That's the trickiest.
tables.DIALOGUE.trainer.14.1: You'll see it get scared. …Don't get used to cutting down a frightened opponent.
tables.DIALOGUE.haran.9.0: A hundred rooms, and not one doorknob worn down.
tables.DIALOGUE.haran.9.1: Means no one ever lived here. An innkeeper looks at the doorknobs first.
tables.DIALOGUE.haran.10.0: I kept rooms empty for the people who went below. If they're not used, they just stay empty.
tables.DIALOGUE.haran.11.0: More guests lately. People come to see the machines.
tables.DIALOGUE.haran.11.1: Word must be getting around far away. Chimneys can be seen from a long way off.
tables.DIALOGUE.haran.12.0: These nights, the glasses tremble on their own. I didn't touch them.
tables.DIALOGUE.haran.12.1: It's the ground crying. Not the drink.
tables.DIALOGUE.haran.13.0: No charge for a room today for anyone going below. Pay when you get back.
tables.DIALOGUE.haran.13.1: That's the only charm I know.
tables.DIALOGUE.haran.14.0: The number who came back equals the number who went out. First day like this, ever.
tables.DIALOGUE.haran.14.1: I won't lock the door tonight.
tables.DIALOGUE.seira.9.0: The steel in this city won't stretch no matter how you hammer it. Its shape is already fixed.
tables.DIALOGUE.seira.9.1: Changing shapes is my whole job, and here there's nothing to change.
tables.DIALOGUE.seira.10.0: Bring me just one thing from the Foundry. I want to take it apart and see inside.
tables.DIALOGUE.seira.10.1: You can't judge a maker's craft from the outside — you have to look inside.
tables.DIALOGUE.seira.11.0: Thanks to the windmill I keep the fire going at night. Thought I could forge in my sleep.
tables.DIALOGUE.seira.11.1: …Then that thought scared me a little. Working in your sleep is what machines do.
tables.DIALOGUE.seira.12.0: They say those things down there copy themselves. It takes me a day to forge one piece.
tables.DIALOGUE.seira.12.1: But I get to name what I make. They can't do that, can they.
tables.DIALOGUE.seira.13.0: What does thousand-year-old iron look like? …I know I shouldn't be curious.
tables.DIALOGUE.seira.14.0: Borin hung up a blueprint. A drawing of a person, apparently.
tables.DIALOGUE.seira.14.1: I stood in front of it a long time. First time I've seen something I can't forge.
tables.DIALOGUE.kade.9.0: People didn't build this city. So who did? Finding that out is my job.
tables.DIALOGUE.kade.9.1: Seen the passage under the fountain? You can't see the bottom. …Not a good sign, but I'm thrilled.
tables.DIALOGUE.kade.10.0: Know what the Overseer said at the end? "The first in 1,140 days."
tables.DIALOGUE.kade.10.1: It didn't wait a thousand years — it counted a thousand years. That's even creepier.
tables.DIALOGUE.kade.11.0: See? Just pull the power line and it's over. Told you it's no big deal.
tables.DIALOGUE.kade.11.1: …Mira didn't look happy hearing that. I know. It just happened to be no big deal this time.
tables.DIALOGUE.kade.12.0: No one to approve the expansion means auto-approval. By the rules.
tables.DIALOGUE.kade.12.1: It's not the fault of whoever wrote the rules. They just never wrote down that they'd be gone.
tables.DIALOGUE.kade.13.0: Hepha understood “stop.” Understood it, and still didn't stop.
tables.DIALOGUE.kade.13.1: I thought about what I'd have done… I don't think I'd have stopped either.
tables.DIALOGUE.kade.14.0: It's not a machine blueprint. It's a blueprint for a person. Even where the heart goes is written down.
tables.DIALOGUE.kade.14.1: I'm not going to check whether we're in those blueprints. Either way, today's work doesn't change.
tables.ENEMIES.cartwraith.d: It rolls in though no one pushes it. Embers still burn inside.
tables.ENEMIES.frostbound.d: It walks toward you, frozen inside the ice. The ice won't say what it came to do.
tables.ENEMIES.jarhusk.d: What was inside the jar. No one broke the seal — which means it came out on its own.
tables.ENEMIES.ventspitter.d: It lived in a spore vent. Whether the vent is the worm's home or the worm is the vent, no one knows.
tables.ENEMIES.sacling.d: Something that came out of an egg sac. Not fully grown yet.
tables.ENEMIES.tide_warden.n: Tide Warden · What the Water Erased
tables.ENEMIES.lost_miner.n: The One Who Couldn't Come Up
tables.ENEMIES.shaft_maw.n: The Thing That Filled the Shaft
tables.EVENTS.bloodmoon.d: The moon is red. Tonight, you shouldn't be outside.
tables.EVENTS.sandstorm.d: The dunes move whole. You can barely see ahead.
tables.EVENTS.sporebloom.d: The whole vale exhaled at once.
tables.EVENTS.rain.d: Rain lashes down. The creatures are fiercer than usual.
tables.ITEMS.sword_wood.d: A practice sword found in a corner of father's storehouse.
tables.ITEMS.sword_iron.d: Standard issue from the Ashen village smithy.
tables.ITEMS.sword_bone.d: A low laugh sounds with every swing.
tables.ITEMS.sword_mythril.d: A blue afterimage trails its arc.
tables.ITEMS.sword_dawn.d: Clears away the night in a single stroke.
tables.ITEMS.scythe_void.d: Where it cuts, stars show for a moment.
tables.ITEMS.bow_storm.d: Release the string and the wind goes first.
tables.ITEMS.bow_starfall.d: A bowstring made from a shard of the fallen star.
tables.ITEMS.staff_branch.d: Pressed into your hand by the village witch.
tables.ITEMS.staff_abyss.d: A crystal grown where the star sleeps.
tables.ITEMS.pick_copper.d: Can mine stone, ice, copper and iron.
tables.ITEMS.pick_sharp.d: Mines the same as a copper pickaxe, but its honed edge hits harder.
tables.ITEMS.pick_iron.d: Can mine gold, crystal and mithril.
tables.ITEMS.pick_mythril.d: Can mine obsidian, soulstone and hellstone.
tables.ITEMS.rod_basic.d: Right-click a water block to cast. Raw meat is used as bait automatically.
tables.ITEMS.rod_adv.d: Quicker bites, and you read them better through your fingertips. Things other than fish get hooked often, too.
tables.ITEMS.fish_common.d: Common, but full of tough little bones.
tables.ITEMS.fish_deep.d: It has eyes that shouldn't belong at this depth.
tables.ITEMS.tank_air.d: A worn tank worn on the back. Lets you hold your breath longer, but it's a little heavy.
tables.ITEMS.tank_deep.d: A tank double-wrapped to endure the depths. Made by stripping and rewinding a portable tank.
tables.ITEMS.tank_abyss.d: Wrings air out anew with a core. Even changes how fast you get winded out of the water.
tables.ITEMS.ring_angler.d: Someone claims to have caught this without any bait. No one believes them.
tables.ITEMS.tide_pearl.d: Found in shells that open only as the tide turns. Rarer still since the ash came down.
tables.ITEMS.sunken_coin.d: The face is worn smooth; whose it was, no one can tell. Still worth something.
tables.ITEMS.lantern_fry.d: Swallow it and your belly glows for a while. You can see in the dark.
tables.ITEMS.river_scale.d: Stitched in layers, it makes armor that won't get wet.
tables.ITEMS.drowned_cell.d: Something the Foundry let wash into the waterways. Dry it out and it still works.
tables.ITEMS.coolant_vial.d: Foundry coolant in a vial. Drink it and your body cools as your hands quicken.
tables.ITEMS.rust_sinker.d: A lump of lead with rivets hammered in. Knock off the rust and it's good again.
tables.ITEMS.knot_angler.d: No one knows who tied it, or when. It won't come undone, and it won't break.
tables.ITEMS.spear_river.d: Unusually long, since it was made for throwing underwater. Works well on land, too.
tables.ITEMS.bow_reed.d: Reeds grown at the water's edge bend easily and spring back.
tables.ITEMS.staff_current.d: Tells you where the water wants to go. Whatever it hits goes that way too.
tables.ITEMS.harpoon_cool.d: A tool the Foundry used to spike overheated things and cool them. Not made to be used on people.
tables.ITEMS.gun_pressure.d: Fires water drawn thin as a thread. They say it cut steel that way.
tables.ITEMS.staff_deluge.d: It was the handle that opened the floodgates. Even then, they knew what would come when it opened.
tables.ITEMS.mariner_compass.d: The needle points not north but to land. They say it has never once been wrong.
tables.ITEMS.charm_float.d: It won't sink. Wear it, and neither will your feet.
tables.ITEMS.ring_ripple.d: Once thrown, it spreads to the very end. And it never comes back.
tables.ITEMS.amul_river.d: River scales strung in layers. Cold things glance right off.
tables.ITEMS.charm_conden.d: Pried from a Foundry cooling tower. Water still beads inside.
tables.ITEMS.ring_sluice.d: Made for closing, so while you wear it, anything closes easily.
tables.ITEMS.amul_undertow.d: The surface is calm. What drags you down lies beneath.
tables.ITEMS.chest_river.d: It won't get wet. Perhaps natural, since it was made from what was fished out of the water.
tables.ITEMS.band_worn.d: Someone wore this for a long time. Still usable, though.
tables.ITEMS.charm_cloud.d: Lets you leap once more in midair.
tables.ITEMS.charm_star.d: A piece of the fallen star's heart.
tables.ITEMS.bag_pouch.d: A small pouch loosely woven from spider silk. Still better than nothing.
tables.ITEMS.bag_satchel.d: A sturdy satchel from a blacksmith's hands.
tables.ITEMS.bag_pack.d: So light it's as if half its weight vanished.
tables.ITEMS.bag_vault.d: It's bigger on the inside than the outside. No one knows how it was made.
tables.ITEMS.egg_common.d: You won't know what hatches until it cracks.
tables.ITEMS.egg_rare.d: You sense the presence of a rare beast.
tables.ITEMS.egg_epic.d: Something is beating quietly inside the egg.
tables.ITEMS.glacium_ore.d: Found only deep in the glacier. Holding it makes your fingertips ache.
tables.ITEMS.tide_ore.d: Embedded in seabed rock. It never dries.
tables.ITEMS.glacium_bar.d: Melting it only makes it colder.
tables.ITEMS.tide_bar.d: Every hammer blow leaves a ripple pattern.
tables.ITEMS.meteorite.d: A lump of iron fallen from the sky. Warm in your palm, as if it hasn't cooled yet.
tables.ITEMS.star_crystal.d: Grows only where a meteor fell. Brighter at night.
tables.ITEMS.det_metal.d: Nearby ore veins show up on the minimap (30-tile radius). Press a utility key (default Z · X) to send out a detection pulse — for 10 seconds, ore behind walls shows on screen too. A little heavy to carry around.
tables.ITEMS.det_mob.d: Nearby creatures show up on the minimap (30-tile radius). Press a utility key (default Z · X) to send out a detection pulse — for 10 seconds, monsters behind walls show on screen too. Shows even what you'd rather not see.
tables.ITEMS.coconut.d: Water fills the hard shell. Found only on islands.
tables.ITEMS.pet_candy.d: Keep it in your pocket and the little ones know before you do.
tables.ITEMS.wildflower.d: Blooms everywhere in forests and meadows.
tables.ITEMS.weed.d: Pull it and pull it, and it grows right back.
tables.ITEMS.cactus_flesh.d: Holds moisture even in parched land.
tables.ITEMS.limestone.d: A soft, pale stone. Stalactites grow where water seeps through it.
tables.ITEMS.granite.d: Stone hardened deep underground. Coarse-grained and tough.
tables.ITEMS.torch.d: Darkness is no good hunting ground.
tables.ITEMS.star_heart.d: You need to gather all five.
tables.ITEMS.ash_feather.d: Crows were the first to adapt to the Ashfall.
tables.ITEMS.bow_crow.d: Light feathers — the string snaps back fast.
tables.ITEMS.dagger_venom.d: It kills slowly, but it kills surely.
tables.ITEMS.bow_silk.d: Whatever it hits gets tangled in thread and slows down.
tables.ITEMS.axe_frost.d: Hits big in one blow, then freezes.
tables.ITEMS.staff_moss.d: Takes back a little of whatever it cuts.
tables.ITEMS.hammer_lava.d: Every blow melts the floor for an instant.
tables.ITEMS.staff_archive.d: Merely reading it sends the verses flying.
tables.ITEMS.charm_lamp.d: Holding it brightens your surroundings a little.
tables.ITEMS.charm_hawk.d: The claw of one whose eyes were unusually sharp even among wolves.
tables.ITEMS.ring_brand.d: It was lodged in the Ash Golem's chest.
tables.ITEMS.relic_frostpane.d: Trapped in ice, yet still fogged. Someone wiped it from the inside.
tables.ITEMS.relic_sundial.d: The needle has stopped at noon. People say it's the hour the star fell.
tables.ITEMS.relic_lastlamp.d: The wick is still there. Whoever lit it never made it back up.
tables.ITEMS.relic_rotcore.d: Only this stayed whole in the middle of the Lair. The blight grew around it.
tables.ITEMS.relic_sporebell.d: Shake it and spores come out instead of sound. The whole grotto grew up hearing it.
tables.ITEMS.relic_frostmark.d: A cast of a handprint pressed into the wall. It has only four fingers.
tables.ITEMS.relic_mazeeye.d: Look into it and the path behind you appears. It never shows the path ahead.
tables.ITEMS.relic_hollowseed.d: No sound when shaken. The tablet said it must not be planted.
tables.ITEMS.cave_moss.d: Grew where no light reaches, drinking only water. Cold and damp to the touch.
tables.ITEMS.moss_poultice.d: Restores 110 HP and heals slowly for a while. Made by pounding four Cave Moss.
tables.ITEMS.pulse_shard.d: Broken off the wall of an awakened ruin. It still beats in your palm.
tables.ITEMS.tonic_hush.d: Drink it inside a ruin to calm the Pulse by 40. Does nothing outside a ruin.
tables.ITEMS.drum_pulse.d: Beat it inside a ruin to raise the Pulse by 35. The ruin must be awake to call the Echo.
tables.ITEMS.seal_mine.d: Proof you searched every corner of the Abandoned Mine. In any ruin, the Pulse rises a quarter slower.
tables.ITEMS.seal_ice.d: Proof you searched every corner of the Ice Dungeon. When a ruin wakes (stage 2 and up), your body hardens like ice.
tables.ITEMS.seal_pyramid.d: Proof you searched every corner of the Pyramid. Chests opened while the Pulse is beating get one extra tier of bonus.
tables.ITEMS.seal_spore.d: Proof you searched every corner of the Spore Grotto. Foes felled inside a ruin calm the Pulse twice as much.
tables.ITEMS.seal_blight.d: Proof you searched every corner of the Blighted Nest. Damage +20% while a ruin is in Frenzy.
tables.ITEMS.seal_abyss.d: Proof you searched every corner of the Sunken Ruins. Echo Trial rewards are increased by half.
tables.ITEMS.ruinmap_ice.d: A gorge map drawn on leather. A hole is punched through at a single spot.
tables.ITEMS.ruinmap_spore.d: Less a map than a record of smells. It says to go where it's strongest.
tables.ITEMS.ruinmap_blight.d: The mapmaker's hand began to shake partway. The line breaks off at the eastern edge.
tables.ITEMS.sword_aether.d: It has no weight. As if the wind were holding it, not your hand.
tables.ITEMS.bow_gale.d: Above the clouds, arrows don't fall.
tables.ITEMS.staff_storm.d: The thunder always comes one beat late.
tables.ITEMS.sword_first.d: Forged before the star first fell.
tables.ITEMS.charm_feather.d: Hold jump while falling to drift down slowly.
tables.ITEMS.charm_zenith.d: Something a wind spirit wore wrapped around itself.
tables.ITEMS.storm_amber.d: Cloud sap hardened in an instant by lightning. The lightning trapped inside still flickers faintly.
tables.ITEMS.cloud_pearl.d: Grows inside cloud jellies. Held in your hand, it tries to float up as if weightless.
tables.ITEMS.rune_frag.d: One comes from each of the three ruins' Stone Tablets.
tables.ITEMS.ruin_key.d: Opens the sealed door of the deep ruin.
tables.ITEMS.charm_dawn.d: Made by hardening the light of the first morning after the Ashfall lifted.
tables.ITEMS.star_whole.d: The five shards hold on to one another. Your palm stays hot.
tables.ITEMS.sum_storm.d: Only sounds atop a Sky Island.
tables.ITEMS.sum_keeper.d: Use it in the deepest part of the ruin.
tables.ITEMS.sum_pursuer.d: Raise it high, and the one that was chasing finally knows which way to go.
tables.ITEMS.power_core.d: Still warm. It hasn't cooled in hundreds of years.
tables.ITEMS.blueprint_frag.d: It's readable — but it describes not how to make things, but how to make things make things.
tables.ITEMS.blueprint_core.d: “Do not use human labor. That is all we learned.”
tables.ITEMS.gear_basic.d: As long as it has a partner to mesh with, it will turn again anytime.
tables.ITEMS.pick_drill.d: The grip trembles on its own. For now, you still have to hold it by hand.
tables.ITEMS.coal.d: Found everywhere. Doesn't burn for long.
tables.ITEMS.lead_bar.d: Heavy and soft. You need it to make batteries.
tables.ITEMS.crude_oil.d: Comes only from the bloodstone beneath the dunes. Too precious to burn as is.
tables.ITEMS.refined_oil.d: Does the work of six or seven lumps of coal on its own.
tables.ITEMS.polymer.d: Comes out alongside refined crude. It neither melts nor freezes.
tables.ITEMS.fuel_brick.d: Five lumps of coal pressed into a single brick.
tables.ITEMS.circuit.d: Thin gold lines run across it like a maze.
tables.ITEMS.motor.d: Give it electricity and it turns on its own. Until you tell it to stop.
tables.ITEMS.machine_frame.d: The skeleton of a large machine. Most factory equipment is built on top of one.
tables.ITEMS.battery_empty.d: Leave it in a battery bank and it charges again.
tables.ITEMS.battery_cell.d: When powered gear runs out of charge, one is slotted in automatically for 200 charge. Standing by a power pole also charges from the grid.
tables.ITEMS.station_work.d: Set it down anywhere and that spot becomes a workshop. Upgrades stack separately on each one you place.
tables.ITEMS.station_forge.d: A brick-built furnace. You need it to melt ore.
tables.ITEMS.crate_wood.d: 24 slots. Just a chest to put things in — no belts or power required.
tables.ITEMS.crate_gold.d: 48 slots. Rimmed in gold, it holds twice as much.
tables.ITEMS.door_wood.d: The hinge goes on the side you face when you hang it. It opens toward that side.
tables.ITEMS.pick_arc.d: Bores through everything but bedrock. Consumes charge.
tables.ITEMS.saw_auto.d: It doesn't stop. Keeps spinning for a while even after you let go.
tables.ITEMS.gun_rail.d: Fires charge, not bullets. A wall or so doesn't count.
tables.ITEMS.charm_cap.d: Increases the charge you carry. Lets you use powered gear longer.
tables.ITEMS.charm_conduit.d: A prototype Kade quietly slipped you.
tables.ITEMS.thatch.d: Cheap and warm. Mind the fire.
tables.ITEMS.rooftile.d: Lay it once and it lasts to your grandchildren.
tables.ITEMS.timberwall.d: A wall with plaster packed between the posts.
tables.ITEMS.wallstone.d: Stones as tall as a person, dressed and stacked.
tables.ITEMS.battlement.d: Notched so you can hide and look out.
tables.ITEMS.window.d: Lets the light in, keeps the wind out.
tables.ITEMS.lamppost.d: Being able to see the road at night matters more than you'd think.
tables.ITEMS.haybale.d: You won't get hurt landing on it.
tables.ITEMS.sandbag.d: A barricade stacked in a hurry.
tables.ITEMS.hoe_iron.d: Right-click dirt or grass to till it. Plant seeds on tilled soil.
tables.ITEMS.scythe_iron.d: Cut ripe crops with this and the grain stays whole. Hit them with any other tool and it all gets crushed.
tables.ITEMS.scythe_star.d: The blade is steeped in stardust. Each cut brings along one more ripe yield.
tables.ITEMS.seed_starroot.d: A root vegetable that only sprouted near the fallen star.
tables.ITEMS.seed_ashcap.d: Grows well even in the dark.
tables.ITEMS.seed_bloodbean.d: A seed made by hardening slime gel. Smells of gel.
tables.ITEMS.seed_bonebloom.d: Someone packed bone meal together and it sprouted. Nobody knows why.
tables.ITEMS.seed_frostherb.d: The soil where it's planted freezes white.
tables.ITEMS.seed_emberpod.d: Lukewarm to the touch. Water them and steam rises.
tables.ITEMS.bloodbean.d: Boiled, it turns the broth red. The taste is surprisingly mild.
tables.ITEMS.bonebloom.d: The petals are white and hard as bone. Ground up, they make medicine.
tables.ITEMS.frostherb.d: Your hands go cold picking it even in midsummer.
tables.ITEMS.emberpod.d: Shell it and out come kernels that are still burning.
tables.ITEMS.fertilizer.d: Right-click a crop to grow it one stage.
tables.ITEMS.food_bread.d: Raises HP regen and VIT for 5 minutes.
tables.ITEMS.food_pie.d: Raises STR and damage for 5 minutes.
tables.ITEMS.food_mstew.d: Raises mana regen and INT for 5 minutes.
tables.ITEMS.food_jelly.d: Raises move speed and DEX for 5 minutes.
tables.ITEMS.food_feast.d: Raises all stats for 10 minutes. Proof that the village is alive.
tables.ITEMS.charm_delver.d: Sized only for one who has searched all five ruins.
tables.ITEMS.core_shard.d: Still lukewarm. Held in the hand, it beats like a pulse.
tables.ITEMS.sword_arc.d: Current drawn from the Proliferator's core runs along the blade. Even a graze sends things flying.
tables.ITEMS.stop_core.d: Something with just “Stop” written into it, very large. What the Foundry never made in the end.
tables.ITEMS.hepha_heart.d: It stayed warm long after it stopped.
tables.ITEMS.charm_govern.d: When things get too fast, it slows itself down. That's all it does.
tables.ITEMS.hammer_still.d: Whatever it hits can do nothing for a moment. Not a weapon for breaking — a weapon for stopping.
tables.ITEMS.archestone.d: No cut marks. It looks as if it had this shape from the very beginning.
tables.ITEMS.draft_glass.d: A blueprint floats inside. What it's a blueprint of can't be read.
tables.ITEMS.proto_ash.d: When something never fully assembled breaks, only this remains.
tables.ITEMS.atelier_key.d: Hepha's heart, melted and hardened again. To get past the wall, you needed something the wall had made.
tables.ITEMS.arche_core.d: The center of the first thing made in the image of a person. Still lukewarm, like a person.
tables.ITEMS.blade_arche.d: A blade that existed only in blueprints and was never forged. In the end, we were the first to make it.
tables.ITEMS.tome_origin.d: The first page reads — “You who read this are not us. That is all right.”
tables.ITEMS.charm_maker.d: A mark that records not what you made, but whether you knew when to stop.
tables.ITEMS.orbit_plate.d: A plate that keeps floating things afloat. Held in the hand, it's just slightly lighter.
tables.ITEMS.orbit_gear.d: A gear that has never stopped. Set it down and it turns very slowly on its own.
