tables.ITEMS.void_lens.d: Look through it and you can see where the star fled. After looking, you won't sleep for a while.
tables.ITEMS.star_ash.d: Comes only from what returned to the sky once and then fell again.
tables.ITEMS.lance_orbit.d: Where it pierces is pulled upward for a moment. The force that kept the citadel aloft, packed into the spearpoint.
tables.ITEMS.bow_meridian.d: It flies not where you aim, but where what you aimed at is going to pass.
tables.ITEMS.charm_orbit.d: Slows falling things a little. Exactly the way the citadel stayed aloft for a thousand years.
tables.ITEMS.deep_alloy.d: Hardens only below the underworld. Neither hot nor cold — which is somehow worse.
tables.ITEMS.miner_tag.d: The name has been scratched out. Only numbers remain — three digits, three times.
tables.ITEMS.gloom_pearl.d: It reflects no light. Stare into it and your eyes can't focus.
tables.ITEMS.drill_abyss.d: It even scrapes bedrock. Scrapes — but never breaks through.
tables.ITEMS.hammer_cave.d: One swing and the ceiling flinches first.
tables.ITEMS.charm_lamp2.d: A lamp that stayed lit to the very end. Whoever carried it never made it back up.
tables.ITEMS.jetpack.d: Hold jump to rise. Up to 30 tiles above the ground, up to 4 seconds at a time. After that it needs to cool.
tables.ITEMS.spear_reed.d: One thrust, and you've made distance first.
tables.ITEMS.mace_iron.d: Solves problems with weight instead of finesse.
tables.ITEMS.dagger_frost.d: An ice wolf's claw, ground down and honed as is.
tables.ITEMS.spear_venom.d: A scorpion's venom stinger fixed to the spearpoint.
tables.ITEMS.mace_thorn.d: The thorns dig in with every blow.
tables.ITEMS.mace_lava.d: A lump of iron that never cools, hung whole on a haft.
tables.ITEMS.dagger_void.d: Takes back as much as it cuts.
tables.ITEMS.spear_storm.d: Wrapped in a wind spirit's feathers. Fast as if thrown.
tables.ITEMS.mace_ruin.d: The last thing left by the hands that guarded the ruin.
tables.ITEMS.crossbow_bone.d: Lashed together crudely from bone, but the string is taut.
tables.ITEMS.bow_venom.d: No need to poison the arrows. The bow itself is poison.
tables.ITEMS.crossbow_iron.d: Slow, but whatever it hits goes down.
tables.ITEMS.bow_ash.d: Release the string and ash scatters.
tables.ITEMS.bow_void.d: It has no string. Just pretend to draw and it fires.
tables.ITEMS.gun_scrap.d: A barrel the Foundry threw away, with a new grip attached.
tables.ITEMS.crossbow_first.d: What the First Keeper kept standing by its door.
tables.ITEMS.orb_ember.d: A single undying ember sealed inside an orb.
tables.ITEMS.tome_bone.d: Open it and you hear the voices of the dead.
tables.ITEMS.orb_venom.d: Poison that spreads like mist, compressed into an orb.
tables.ITEMS.tome_ash.d: Sparks leak out from between the pages.
tables.ITEMS.orb_storm.d: Your fingertips tingle while you hold it.
tables.ITEMS.tome_void.d: The more you read, the more pages vanish.
tables.ITEMS.orb_core.d: A shard of the Proliferator's core, still pulsing.
tables.ITEMS.tome_first.d: The only book that records the night the star first fell.
tables.ITEMS.spear_tide.d: Shaped for cutting through currents. A bit heavy on land.
tables.ITEMS.blade_shark.d: Rows of teeth set into it. If one falls out, just set another.
tables.ITEMS.bow_harpoon.d: It had a line attached, but no one ever reels it back.
tables.ITEMS.orb_abyss.d: Holds water from a place light has never reached.
tables.ITEMS.helm_diver.d: Helps you hold your breath longer. You can't hear much, though.
tables.ITEMS.boots_fin.d: Underwater, gliding is faster than walking.
tables.ITEMS.ring_pearl.d: The shorter your breath, the brighter it shines.
tables.ITEMS.charm_ink.d: Learned from an octopus how to vanish and reappear.
tables.ITEMS.amul_scale.d: Scales strung one at a time. Underwater, your breath feels a little less urgent.
tables.ITEMS.charm_bell.d: A piece that broke off the bell. It still rings, very faintly.
tables.ITEMS.ring_deep.d: They say you mustn't fall asleep in the deep. This helps you endure the opposite.
tables.ITEMS.sigil_current.d: Carved by someone who knew where the current goes.
tables.ITEMS.mace_bell.d: What once struck the bell. With every swing, the water rings first.
tables.ITEMS.harpoon_lamp.d: A harpoon with a lantern tied on. Fired in the dark, you can see its path.
tables.ITEMS.bag_abyss.d: Double-sealed so no water gets in. Being bigger inside than out was learned from the ruin coffer.
tables.ITEMS.pick_abyss.d: Mines with crushing force. Breaks everything but bedrock.
tables.ITEMS.hammer_tide.d: Swing it and the water goes first. Even on land.
tables.ITEMS.gun_harpoon.d: They did away with the retrieval line altogether. It fires that much faster.
tables.ITEMS.tome_abyss.d: There were letters even where light has never reached.
tables.ITEMS.chest_abyss.d: Made to withstand deep-water pressure, so a hit on land is nothing.
tables.ITEMS.charm_core.d: A single piece of abyssal core, attached as is. Always lukewarm.
tables.ITEMS.fern_frond.d: Carpets the jungle floor. Crush it and it gives off a strong smell.
tables.ITEMS.orchid.d: The darker it is, the more vivid its bloom.
tables.ITEMS.lily_pad.d: Floats on the surface of the waterfall lake.
tables.ITEMS.leaf_oak.d: A broad leaf from the Ashen Forest. Dusted with ash.
tables.ITEMS.leaf_pine.d: Needles that stay green even in the snow. They smell of resin.
tables.ITEMS.leaf_jungle.d: Wider than two palms put together. Rainwater pools on it.
tables.ITEMS.leaf_corrupt.d: A leaf curled up and turned violet. Your fingertips tingle when you touch it.
tables.ITEMS.leaf_sky.d: A leaf split into a star shape. It sways even without wind.
tables.ITEMS.leaf_palm.d: A long leaf split like a feather. Weave them and you get a roof.
tables.ITEMS.crab_shell.d: Thick and light. Used as armor lining.
tables.ITEMS.shark_tooth.d: Teeth that fall out and grow back. No matter how much you grind, they never dull.
tables.ITEMS.ink_sac.d: Burst it and the water turns to night.
tables.ITEMS.abyss_pearl.d: Too bright for something sunlight has never touched.
tables.ITEMS.kelp.d: Tough. Braid it and you get rope.
tables.ITEMS.sea_salt.d: What's left when you boil down seabed sand.
tables.ITEMS.sulfur.d: Embedded in glacier and seabed rock. Don't strike a match near it.
tables.ITEMS.gunpowder.d: Sulfur and salt ground up with charcoal. It all depends on how you handle it.
tables.ITEMS.bomb_small.d: Light the fuse and throw. Once lit, there's no taking it back.
tables.ITEMS.bomb_big.d: Double the gunpowder. Step back after throwing.
tables.ITEMS.bomb_dig.d: It wasn't made to hurt people. It was made to get rid of walls.
tables.ITEMS.pressure_plate_m.d: Plates layered and wrapped to withstand deep-water pressure.
tables.ITEMS.abyss_core.d: Pearls and pressure plates pressed together into one. The heart of tier-4 machines.
tables.ITEMS.keeper_seal.d: It doesn't say who was trying to lock away what.
tables.ITEMS.sum_tide.d: Ring it on the seabed. The water answers in its place.
tables.ITEMS.glowcap.d: Keeps glowing for a while even after it's picked.
tables.ITEMS.food_curry.d: Raises fire resistance and STR for 5 minutes.
tables.ITEMS.potion_glow.d: Lights up your surroundings for 8 minutes.
tables.ITEMS.potion_glow_greater.d: Lights up a wider area around you for 15 minutes.
tables.ITEMS.charm_canopy.d: The claw of something that leapt between the branches.
tables.ITEMS.charm_spore.d: In your hand it keeps brightening and dimming, as if breathing.
tables.ITEMS.sum_slime.d: Use it on the surface and the Slime King will come.
tables.ITEMS.sum_heart.d: Use it in the Blighted Land.
tables.ITEMS.neverthaw.d: Doesn't melt even when taken out of the Ice Dungeon. Hold it and your hand cools first.
tables.ITEMS.warden_seal.d: It doesn't say what it was given to guard. Only that it was guarded.
tables.ITEMS.sealed_ash.d: The ash in the jar is still warm. No one has ever broken the seal.
tables.ITEMS.caged_sun.d: Written on the wall: the sun wasn't carved here — it was caged.
tables.ITEMS.deep_ember.d: An ember left in a mine lamp. This fire didn't go out even after the shafts were abandoned.
tables.ITEMS.foreman_tag.d: The name has been scratched out. Erased by the last one left.
tables.ITEMS.blight_spawn.d: Something still moves inside. Hold it too long and your hand goes numb.
tables.ITEMS.nest_crown.d: Woven from bone, and not a single one of them human.
tables.ITEMS.spore_dust.d: You have to hold your breath while collecting it. Breathe, and it starts growing inside you.
tables.ITEMS.cap_signet.d: The Spore Grotto has no door. And yet there was something used to open it.
tables.ITEMS.pet_ember_squirrel.d: Unbothered even with embers on its tail.
tables.ITEMS.pet_glass_moth.d: Its wings chime like glass when they touch.
tables.ITEMS.pet_pebble_kin.d: When it stops rolling, it just looks like a stone.
tables.ITEMS.pet_dust_sparrow.d: Flies on ahead, shaking off ash.
tables.ITEMS.pet_ash_owl.d: Sees clearly through the ash even at night.
tables.ITEMS.pet_cinder_toad.d: Its throat puffs up red with every breath.
tables.ITEMS.pet_thorn_wisp.d: Leaves tiny thorns wherever it brushes past.
tables.ITEMS.pet_star_sprite.d: Drawn in by the starlight in your right hand.
tables.ITEMS.pet_ember_drake.d: Can't fly yet, but has a quick temper.
tables.ITEMS.pet_void_hatchling.d: Look into it and you're the one who looks away first.
tables.ITEMS.pet_storm_falcon.d: When it dives, the sound arrives one beat late.
tables.MACHINE.belt.d: Moves items forward one tile per second. Needs no power. Waits in place if the way ahead is blocked.
tables.MACHINE.pole.d: Connects machines within 5 tiles to the grid. Poles within 10 tiles of each other link into a single grid.
tables.MACHINE.crate.d: 24-slot storage. Turn on “Output” and it feeds its contents forward one at a time — an input for supplying a factory.
tables.MACHINE.gen.d: Burns fuel to supply power to the grid. Must be within a pole's radius to connect.
tables.MACHINE.battery.d: Stores surplus power and releases it when there's a shortfall. Put depleted batteries in to recharge them.
tables.MACHINE.drill.d: Burns fuel to mine ore veins within 5 tiles on its own (mining grade 2 — coal, copper, iron, lead, gold, mithril, bloodstone). Mines one vein tile more than twenty times; rich deposits never run dry.
tables.MACHINE.drill_e.d: A drill powered by electricity. Three times faster than the mechanical kind, with a wider radius (mining grade 3 — soulstone, hellstone, ether, power stone, meteorite, plus gold and mithril deposits). Can't mine anything above grade 4 (Act 3 ores, ruin glass).
tables.MACHINE.drill_x.d: The top tier of the electric drill, wrapped in pressure plates. Mining grade 5 — mines Act 3 ores like cryolite and tidestone, plus cores and design glass. Faster with a wider radius than the electric drill, but uses nearly twice the power.
tables.MACHINE.pump.d: Extracts crude oil if there's bloodstone within 4 tiles. Doesn't consume the bloodstone, so it never runs dry.
tables.MACHINE.smelter.d: Burns fuel to melt ore into ingots. A first-generation machine that runs without power.
tables.MACHINE.press.d: Presses to increase density. Coal into fuel bricks, ingots into steel plates.
tables.MACHINE.refinery.d: Splits crude oil into refined oil and polymer. Yields three times as much as doing it by hand.
tables.MACHINE.assembler.d: Fits parts together. Picks and makes whatever it can from the materials you load.
tables.MACHINE.sorter.d: Sends only the chosen item forward and passes the rest to the side, clockwise. Splits a mixed stream of ore.
tables.MACHINE.turret.d: Eats rivets and shoots enemies in range on its own. Feed it ammo by belt and it needs no tending.
tables.MACHINE.trap.d: Fries enemies that step on it. The player doesn't get shocked.
tables.MACHINE.switch.d: Stops and restarts the whole connected grid at once. The first thing to install when you build a factory.
tables.MACHINE.dart.d: Fires darts when something comes within 10 tiles in front. Needs no power.
tables.MACHINE.flamejet.d: Burns whatever gets close. Short range, but leaves a burn.
tables.MACHINE.frostjet.d: Whatever it hits is slowed for a while. Terrifying when set in a narrow passage.
tables.MACHINE.pressor.d: Presses with far more force than a press. Pressure plates and abyssal cores come only from here.
tables.MACHINE.desal.d: Boils down seabed sand and kelp to produce salt and rope.
tables.MACHINE.belt_fast.d: Moves two tiles per second. Mix it freely with regular belts, or swap it in just where bottlenecks form.
tables.MACHINE.battery_hi.d: Holds four battery banks' worth in one tile. Your factory won't stall even after sunset when the wind dies.
tables.MACHINE.windmill.d: Runs without fuel, but needs 14 tiles of open sky above it. The village rooftops are the perfect spot.
tables.MACHINE.mill.d: Grinds grain into flour. Put in bone fragments and you get fertilizer.
tables.MACHINE.oven.d: Cooks by burning firewood. Runs without power, so it's the first machine to go up in a village.
tables.MODES.0.d: You lose some XP and gold. You can recover half where you fell.
tables.MODES.1.d: Monsters have 2× HP and attack. When you die, up to half your bag drops where you fell.
tables.MODES.2.d: Monsters have 5× HP and attack. Die once and the record in this slot is erased.
tables.MYSTIC.well.lines.0: A well with no visible bottom. It holds not water, but something heavier.
tables.MYSTIC.well.lines.1: There are many handprints on the rim. All of them face inward.
tables.MYSTIC.well.got: You feel as if something has been placed on a scale
tables.MYSTIC.echo.lines.0: The room sends sound back. But what comes back isn't the sound you made.
tables.MYSTIC.echo.lines.1: Press your ear to the wall, and words spoken here very long ago are still circling.
tables.MYSTIC.echo.got: You don't know what it said, but your mind feels clearer
tables.MYSTIC.star.lines.0: The ceiling is intact, yet starlight has pooled here.
tables.MYSTIC.star.lines.1: It seems a shard of the fallen star is still lodged somewhere below.
tables.MYSTIC.star.ask: Dip your hand in the light
tables.MYSTIC.star.got: Your body feels lighter and your wounds have closed
tables.MYSTIC.gale.lines.0: Between the pillars, the wind blows in only one direction. Off the island, downward.
tables.MYSTIC.gale.lines.1: Footprints are carved into the floor stones. All face the edge, and none come back.
tables.MYSTIC.gale.ask: Spread your arms and face the wind
tables.MYSTIC.gale.got: Your feet feel lighter — you can jump once more in midair
tables.NPCS.tamer.line: The beasts may be a little shy, but give them an egg and they'll warm up to you fast.
tables.NPCS.trainer.line: Just because the Ashfall lifted doesn't mean you get stronger on your own. You have to put in the work.
tables.NPCS.haran.line: Plenty of rooms. This city still has more rooms than people.
tables.NPCS.seira.line: I leave the item as it is and just change its name. With bad luck, it gets worse.
tables.NPCS.kade.line: People didn't build this city. So who did? Finding that out is my job.
tables.NPCS.pedlar.line: This is all I brought today. Come tomorrow and there'll be something else.
tables.NPCS.yunseul.role: Last Person of the Sunken City
tables.NPCS.yunseul.line: No one who went up ever came back. So I decided not to go up.
tables.NPCS.oreman.line: Mining it is your job, but if you're in a hurry, buy from me. You'll have to pay a bit, of course.
tables.NPCS.armsman.line: I only put out what suits your hands. Selling you something you can't even lift does neither of us any good.
tables.PETS.ember_squirrel.d: Unbothered even with embers on its tail.
tables.PETS.glass_moth.d: Its wings chime like glass when they touch.
tables.PETS.pebble_kin.d: When it stops rolling, it just looks like a stone.
tables.PETS.dust_sparrow.d: Flies on ahead, shaking off ash.
tables.PETS.ash_owl.d: Sees clearly through the ash even at night.
tables.PETS.cinder_toad.d: Its throat puffs up red with every breath.
tables.PETS.thorn_wisp.d: Leaves tiny thorns wherever it brushes past.
tables.PETS.star_sprite.d: Drawn in by the starlight in your right hand.
tables.PETS.ember_drake.d: Can't fly yet, but has a quick temper.
tables.PETS.void_hatchling.d: Look into it and you're the one who looks away first.
tables.PETS.storm_falcon.d: When it dives, the sound arrives one beat late.
tables.PROFS.farm.line: Till, plant, harvest. Grows each time you harvest a fully ripe plot.
tables.PROFS.farm.perks.0.2: Always get back at least one seed when harvesting.
tables.PROFS.farm.perks.2.2: Seeds replant themselves where you harvest.
tables.PROFS.fish.line: Grows with the time you spend waiting by the water. Rises whenever you reel anything in.
tables.PROFS.fish.perks.0.2: The window to strike on a bite extends to 1.6 seconds.
tables.PROFS.fish.perks.1.2: Greatly raises the chance of hooking deep-sea fish.
tables.PROFS.fish.perks.2.2: 25% chance to catch one extra fish.
tables.PULSE_EVENTS.hunt.d: The ruin has marked one — bring it down before it escapes
tables.PULSE_EVENTS.stones.d: Stones ring in three other rooms — touch all three to scatter the Pulse
tables.PULSE_EVENTS.greed.d: A golden chest has risen — open it before it sinks. Its guardian awakens
tables.PULSE_EVENTS.siege.d: The ruin has shut its doors — defeat all three waves that rush in
tables.PULSE_RAGE.ice.t: The fires within the ice go out all at once
tables.PULSE_RAGE.mine.t: The shafts rumble — something is coming down
tables.PULSE_RAGE.pyramid.t: Heated sand pours from the cracks in the walls
tables.PULSE_RAGE.spore.t: The spores in the walls burst all at once
tables.PULSE_RAGE.story0.t: The chamber's frost swallows the fire
tables.PULSE_RAGE.story1.t: The folded path twists — something is coming down
tables.PULSE_RAGE.story2.t: The rooms beneath your feet awaken all at once
tables.RUIN_CARD.ice.line: There were people who froze the gorge themselves. That ice is melting now.
tables.RUIN_CARD.pyramid.line: It isn't a king's tomb. It's an eye built to watch the sky.
tables.RUIN_CARD.mine.line: The shafts are still warm. The last shift never came up.
tables.RUIN_CARD.blight.sub: The Eastern Edge, the Deepest Place
tables.RUIN_CARD.blight.line: From here on, the blight takes the place of walls.
tables.RUIN_CARD.spore.line: There is no entrance. You have to burrow your own way out, too.
tables.RUIN_CARD.story0.line: There's writing beneath the frost. Written by two hands.
tables.RUIN_CARD.story1.line: The paths overlap. You're meant to pass through the same room twice.
tables.RUIN_CARD.story2.line: There's no footing. Whoever came this far had no intention of going back.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.ice.0.1.0: A palm print is frozen on the inside of the wall. The mark of pushing from inside out.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.ice.0.1.1: Not a hand trying to get out — a hand trying to keep something from getting in.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.ice.1.1.0: A stone that used to hold fire. It was broken on purpose.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.ice.1.1.1: Which means they knew the warm things get eaten first.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.ice.2.1.0: The wall is crammed with tally marks. It stops somewhere past three hundred.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.ice.2.1.1: They were counting the years until something would fall.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.pyramid.0.1.0: The hole in the ceiling aims precisely at one point in the sky.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.pyramid.0.1.1: There's nothing in that spot now. A thousand years ago, there was.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.pyramid.1.1.0: Too shallow for a king's coffin. It isn't a place for a person to lie.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.pyramid.1.1.1: Something was laid here, and someone took it.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.pyramid.2.1.0: Every name carved into the wall has been chiseled away.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.pyramid.2.1.1: Those who kept records erased only their own names.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.mine.0.1.0: “Not our shaft past this point” — scratched hastily with a nail.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.mine.0.1.1: Below, sheet metal older than ours runs on.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.mine.1.1.0: A thousand years later and it hasn't rotted. That's the air down here.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.mine.1.1.1: Someone got up mid-meal and went somewhere.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.mine.2.1.0: The scratches on the wall go only upward. They were trying to climb.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.mine.2.1.1: But this is not a wall you can climb.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.blight.0.1.0: Ruin bricks are half-sunk in something soft as flesh.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.blight.0.1.1: Not breaking them down — digesting them. Very slowly.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.blight.1.1.0: The growth rings of a wooden pillar in the wall are missing a single year.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.blight.1.1.1: That year, everything in this land stopped growing.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.blight.2.1.0: The trail of spreading blight suddenly veers at one point.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.blight.2.1.1: The night the star fell, this was startled too.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.root.0.1.0: The roots all stopped and hardened just short of the ceiling.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.root.0.1.1: Nothing grew while something was up above.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.root.1.1.0: Seeds wrapped in cloth and hidden inside the wall. Still alive.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.root.1.1.1: Someone prepared in case the forest could never grow again.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.root.2.1.0: There are many knee prints on the floor. All facing the same way — upward.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.root.2.1.1: It was probably not prayer, but watch.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.spore.0.1.0: Only these spores smell of iron. They grew feeding on what rises from below.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.spore.0.1.1: Which means it's still hot down there.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.spore.1.1.0: Moss clings to human bones and glows on its own.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.spore.1.1.1: It means someone went down — and never came back up.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.spore.2.1.0: Put your hand on the wall and a very slow beat comes through.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.spore.2.1.1: In a thousand years, it hasn't missed a single beat.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.sky.0.1.0: A thick iron ring is set into the island's edge. The chain snapped off, hanging downward.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.sky.0.1.1: The islands weren't floating from the start — they were being held.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.sky.1.1.0: Names were carved into every pillar. The wind erased them first.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.sky.1.1.1: Only the endings remain — and all end with the same word: “-keeper.”
tables.RUIN_HINTS.sky.2.1.0: Every window is cut facing below your feet. This wasn't built for watching the sky.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.sky.2.1.1: It was a place for looking down on the land. Watching for what might fall.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.sky.3.0: A Page of the Storm Log
tables.RUIN_HINTS.sky.3.1.0: “Third storm. Another sentinel did not return.”
tables.RUIN_HINTS.sky.3.1.1: “The altar's orb grows dim. Someone must rekindle it.”
tables.RUIN_HINTS.sky.4.1.0: Dry soil and seed husks remain in a broken jar.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.sky.4.1.1: Something was grown here. Something that won't grow on the ground.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.sky.5.1.0: Tally marks crowd around a circle carved in the floor. One mark per star.
tables.RUIN_HINTS.sky.5.1.1: Only beside the last mark is the groove carved deep — that's the star that fell.
tables.RUIN_LORE.ice.lines.0: “The frost was not a punishment. We covered ourselves with it.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.ice.lines.1: “What rose from below ate the warm things first. So we froze this gorge.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.ice.lines.2: “What is frozen does not grow. What does not grow is not noticed.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.ice.lines.3: “This is as far as we can hold out. We leave it to whoever comes next.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.ice.lines.4: — Beneath it is one more line. Carved not long ago, in a different hand.
tables.RUIN_LORE.ice.lines.5: “Last night fire fell from the sky. What was frozen has begun to thaw.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.pyramid.lines.0: “We did not worship the stars as gods. We watched them.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.pyramid.lines.1: “This tomb is not for a king. It is an eye raised toward the sky.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.pyramid.lines.2: “One star left its orbit. We counted three hundred years until it would fall.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.pyramid.lines.3: “We knew where it would fall, too. The Ashen Forest to the west. So we let no one live there.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.pyramid.lines.4: — And yet now, a village stands on that spot.
tables.RUIN_LORE.mine.lines.0: “On level 8, what came out wasn't wall but sheet metal. Someone dug this far before us.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.mine.lines.1: “The foreman kept telling us to dig. Said it was an order from above.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.mine.lines.2: “Above who? There's no one in the village who'd order something like this.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.mine.lines.3: “Saw the foreman's face today. A light was turning behind the eyes.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.mine.lines.4: — Below this there's no writing. Only fingernail scratches remain.
tables.RUIN_LORE.blight.lines.0: “Blight is not a sickness. It is digestion.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.blight.lines.1: “Something is eating this land very slowly. A handspan every thousand years.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.blight.lines.2: “The night the star fell, the pace of eating changed. As if startled.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.blight.lines.3: “Startled means it didn't know about the star either. It, too, was simply living here.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.blight.lines.4: — Then this land has three masters. Us, it, and what fell.
tables.RUIN_LORE.root.lines.0: “Trees remember. Longer than we do, and more precisely.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.root.lines.1: “Cut into the heartwood and there is a missing ring for that one year, a thousand years ago.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.root.lines.2: “That year, this forest did not grow. It could not.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.root.lines.3: “Because the sky stayed closed the whole year. Something was looking down from above.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.root.lines.4: — And it left. But it is written that it will return.
tables.RUIN_LORE.spore.lines.0: “We do not speak. We only share breath.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.spore.lines.1: “The smell of iron rises from below. Very deep down, something is still turning.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.spore.lines.2: “It has not rested once in a thousand years. It never learned how.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.spore.lines.3: “People made it and then forgot it. What is forgotten cannot stop.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.spore.lines.4: — The reason this vale is so bright is that it is still hot down below.
tables.RUIN_LORE.citadel.lines.1: “In the previous cycle, we sent the star back to the sky. We believed that was right.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.citadel.lines.2: “The returned star was chased again, fled again, and fell again. We ended nothing.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.citadel.lines.3: “The launch coordinates were fixed from the beginning. Reference point — ‘where it first came from.’”
tables.RUIN_LORE.citadel.lines.4: “‘Sending it back’ was the wrong phrase. We only threw it back to where it had been.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.citadel.lines.5: “So this time, we decided to remain below — stamping out the city, drawing the next people.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.citadel.lines.6: “Only this engine we could not shut down. Shutting it down would have meant admitting we were wrong.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.citadel.lines.7: — And it is still ready to launch. Waiting for someone to cancel it.
tables.RUIN_LORE.citadel.lines.9: “Confirmed: no launch this cycle. From the direction of the reference point, for the first time, a response has come.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.citadel.lines.10: — This last line was written in a different hand, very recently.
tables.RUIN_LORE.shaft.lines.0: “The company told us to dig down to level 3.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.shaft.lines.1: “From level 4 we dug because we wanted to. Curious what was below.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.shaft.lines.2: “On level 7 the lamp went out. When we relit it, the tunnel we'd dug was gone.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.shaft.lines.3: “Level 9. No one told us to, but we're still digging. I don't know why anymore.”
tables.RUIN_LORE.shaft.lines.4: — From here on it's not writing, only scratch marks.
tables.SKILLS.s_cleave.d: Slashes in a circle around you for %d%% weapon damage.
tables.SKILLS.s_charge.d: Charges forward, dealing %d%% weapon damage and heavy knockback to enemies hit.
tables.SKILLS.s_guard.d: Reduces damage taken by 55%% and ignores knockback for %d seconds.
tables.SKILLS.s_whirl.d: Spins for 2.5 seconds, dealing %d%% weapon damage per second.
tables.SKILLS.s_quake.d: Strikes the ground, sending shockwaves left and right. %d%% weapon damage and a 2-second slow.
tables.SKILLS.s_warcry.d: Gain Rage and Ironskin for %d seconds and push back nearby enemies.
tables.SKILLS.s_titan.d: While HP is at or below 50%: damage +35%, defense +15.
tables.SKILLS.s_undying.d: When dealt a fatal blow, hold on at 1 HP and recover 25% of max HP. Once every 120 seconds.
tables.SKILLS.s_volley.d: Fires %d arrows in a fan. 70%% weapon damage each.
tables.SKILLS.s_pierce.d: Fires an arrow that pierces enemies. %d%% weapon damage.
tables.SKILLS.s_rain.d: Drops %d arrows on a target location.
tables.SKILLS.s_smoke.d: Bursts a smokescreen for brief invulnerability and faster movement for %d seconds. Nearby enemies are slowed.
tables.SKILLS.s_mark.d: Marks the targeted enemy; it takes +%d%% damage for 10 seconds.
tables.SKILLS.s_hunter.d: Crit damage +80%; on kill, move speed +30% for 3 seconds.
tables.SKILLS.s_tempest.d: Ranged attacks have a 30% chance to loose one extra arrow.
tables.SKILLS.s_fireball.d: An exploding ball of fire. %d damage + INT scaling.
tables.SKILLS.s_nova.d: Freezes nearby enemies, slowing them for 3 seconds and dealing %d damage.
tables.SKILLS.s_heal.d: Instantly restores %d%% HP and regenerates for 5 seconds.
tables.SKILLS.s_barrier.d: Wraps you in a barrier that absorbs up to %d damage (scales with INT). Lasts 20 seconds.
tables.SKILLS.s_wolf.d: Summons %d wolves that fight for 30 seconds.
tables.SKILLS.s_chain.d: Lightning jumps between up to %d enemies, weakening as it goes.
tables.SKILLS.s_blink.d: Teleports toward where you aim and leaves %d damage where you stood.
tables.SKILLS.s_meteor.d: Drops a star where you aim. Heavy damage and burns over a wide area.
tables.STATION_DESC.work.1: Things you can make with planks and nails.
tables.STATION_DESC.work.2: Measures and shapes. Parts start coming out.
tables.STATION_DESC.work.3: A design core sits on top. Now it builds machines that build machines.
tables.STATION_DESC.work.4: Clamps an abyssal core and bonds under pressure. A place to make above water what gets used below it.
tables.STATION_DESC.forge.2: Bellows fitted. Steel plates come out.
tables.STATION_DESC.forge.3: Melts with electricity. Now it runs like a factory.
tables.STATION_DESC.forge.4: Pressurizes the whole furnace to melt. Even salt and pearls become materials.
tables.TABLETS.0.lines.0: “The star does not come to punish. It comes fleeing.”
tables.TABLETS.0.lines.1: “I will not write what it flees from. If I write it, it will read these words.”
tables.TABLETS.0.lines.2: “But this much I record — when the star shatters it becomes five, and each of the five sleeps and dreams.”
tables.TABLETS.0.lines.3: “The dreams make everything around them forget their own names. What you call the Ashfall is that.”
tables.TABLETS.1.lines.0: “We gathered the five. And we sent the star back to the sky.”
tables.TABLETS.1.lines.1: “The Ashfall lifted, and we believed we had won. For a hundred years or so, it truly seemed so.”
tables.TABLETS.1.lines.2: “But what we sent back was the pursued. Not the pursuer.”
tables.TABLETS.1.lines.3: “The star will flee again, and fall again. We ended nothing.”
tables.TABLETS.1.lines.4: “So we raised islands into the sky and posted sentinels. To stop those who would come next.”
tables.TABLETS.2.lines.0: “After raising the sentinels, we chose to sleep. Staying awake was too heavy.”
tables.TABLETS.2.lines.1: “To whoever reads this. Do not wake us. Instead, do better than we did.”
tables.TABLETS.2.lines.2: “What lies beyond the door is not an enemy. It is the greatest mistake we left behind.”
tables.TABLETS.2.lines.3: “If you would take the same path, the Keeper will stop you first. That is its task.”
tables.TABLETS.2.lines.4: “If you have gone beyond it — you have earned the right to make the choice we could not.”
tables.TALK.elara.grave.say.0: Where did you leave it? …No, you don't have to say. It'll be marked on your map.
tables.TALK.elara.grave.say.1: Your things lying somewhere out there — to me, that sounds like you lying somewhere out there.
tables.TALK.elara.grave.re.0.s: It doesn't have to be soon. Just come back.
tables.TALK.elara.grave.re.1.s: If you can, then do. …I haven't been able to let go of anything yet.
tables.TALK.elara.hurt.say.0: Sit. That's not a request, that's the camp keeper talking.
tables.TALK.elara.hurt.say.1: You're not walking right now — you're falling forward.
tables.TALK.elara.hurt.say.2: Don't come in reeking of blood. People here notice.
tables.TALK.elara.hurt.re.0.s: People who are fine don't say that.
tables.TALK.elara.hurt.re.1.s: Go to Borin. Give my name and you'll get one for free.
tables.TALK.elara.bloodmoon.say.0: The moon's red. I've closed the door. You're the only one who'd knock.
tables.TALK.elara.bloodmoon.say.1: On red nights everyone goes quiet. Beasts, people. That's scarier.
tables.TALK.elara.bloodmoon.re.0.t: I still have to go out.
tables.TALK.elara.bloodmoon.re.0.s: I know. Knock when you're back. I'll be awake.
tables.TALK.elara.bloodmoon.re.1.s: …Thank you. I guess I sat up all night waiting to hear that.
tables.TALK.elara.sandstorm.say.0: You can't come in with that much sand stuck to you. Shake it off first.
tables.TALK.elara.sandstorm.say.1: They say the whole desert moved. The wind reached us here.
tables.TALK.elara.sandstorm.re.0.t: Has it calmed down out in the desert?
tables.TALK.elara.sandstorm.re.0.s: It's never been calm. It's just gotten louder lately.
tables.TALK.elara.sporebloom.say.0: Something burst in the vale, I hear. The smell reaches all the way here.
tables.TALK.elara.sporebloom.say.1: Take shallow breaths. Once that smell soaks into your clothes, it lingers.
tables.TALK.elara.sporebloom.re.0.s: Ask Mira. All I know is that it smells.
tables.TALK.elara.rain.say.0: Get under the eaves. This isn't the kind of rain that washes you clean.
tables.TALK.elara.rain.say.1: It's ash melting on the way down. Stand in it long and your clothes rot first.
tables.TALK.elara.rain.re.0.t: The creatures get fierce when it rains.
tables.TALK.elara.rain.re.0.s: Right. On wet days, everyone's temper turns sour. Beasts and people alike.
tables.TALK.elara.chdone.say.0: Your face has eased. You've tied something off.
tables.TALK.elara.chdone.say.1: Today you've got the face of someone who'd answer anything with "done."
tables.TALK.elara.chdone.re.0.s: That's not mine to decide. Still, you can rest for a day.
tables.TALK.elara.broke.say.0: Your pockets are empty. It's all over your face.
tables.TALK.elara.broke.say.1: I didn't want to talk about money, but — you can't buy anything right now, can you.
tables.TALK.elara.broke.re.0.s: I've got none. Check the board instead. Requests always show up before money does.
tables.TALK.elara.rich.say.0: Where'd you get all that gold? …No, I'm not really asking.
tables.TALK.elara.rich.say.1: Your bag looks heavy. Carry heavy things and your feet slow down.
tables.TALK.elara.rich.re.0.s: No need. What's here is enough for me alone. You use it.
tables.TALK.elara.night.say.0: At this hour, only you and I are awake.
tables.TALK.elara.night.say.1: Sound carries far at night. That's why I don't open the door at night.
tables.TALK.elara.night.say.2: I won't tell you to sleep. I don't either.
tables.TALK.elara.night.re.0.s.0: You never know who might come back.
tables.TALK.elara.night.re.0.s.1: Once I locked the door and went to sleep. That night, someone knocked.
tables.TALK.elara.dawn.say.0: The dawn air is the clearest. The ash hasn't risen yet.
tables.TALK.elara.dawn.say.1: When the sun comes up, you can see the tracks of whatever came and went in the night. Clean today.
tables.TALK.elara.dawn.re.0.s: …Thank you for always keeping that promise.
tables.TALK.elara.goal.say.0: Looks like you're all prepared. Only one thing left now.
tables.TALK.elara.goal.say.1: Don't stand in front of the door too long. That's the hardest place to be.
tables.TALK.elara.goal.re.0.s: Being scared is normal. If you weren't, that'd worry me more.
tables.TALK.elara.night2.say.0: I leave the door open at night now. It doesn't scare me anymore.
tables.TALK.elara.night2.say.1: No matter how many times I see a night with the stars back, I can't get used to it.
tables.TALK.elara.night2.re.0.s: …Let's. Wait a moment, let me put out the lantern.
tables.TALK.elara.day2.say.0: Since the star returned to the sky, less ash falls. Noticeably less.
tables.TALK.elara.day2.say.1: People are coming back one by one. This camp won't be a camp for much longer.
tables.TALK.elara.day2.say.2: Have you been over to Dawnhold? The people there don't believe the stories from here.
tables.TALK.elara.day2.re.0.s.0: I have to. People coming back can't be left unable to find the door.
tables.TALK.elara.day2.re.0.s.1: That's the one thing I'm good at.
tables.TALK.elara.day.say.0: Heading out again today? Water flask filled?
tables.TALK.elara.day.say.1: Take a look at the board before you go. I put up something new yesterday.
tables.TALK.elara.day.say.2: I won't tell you to be careful anymore. I know you won't listen.
tables.TALK.elara.day.re.0.s: You decide. I'll just keep the door open.
tables.TALK.borin.grave.say.0: You left your tools behind. Iron left in the ground too long goes bad.
tables.TALK.borin.grave.say.1: If going back there scares you, just tell me where it is. I'll remember it for you.
tables.TALK.borin.grave.re.0.s: I'll make it. But you mine the ore. That much I can't do.
tables.TALK.borin.hurt.say.0: It's not your armor that's dented — it's you.
tables.TALK.borin.hurt.say.1: Hands in that state can't hold anything, let alone a hammer. Sit down.
tables.TALK.borin.hurt.re.0.s: Bring it here. Iron can be mended, but people aren't so simple.
tables.TALK.borin.bloodmoon.say.0: I'm keeping the forge lit tonight. On a red night, firelight is a wall.
tables.TALK.borin.bloodmoon.say.1: When that moon rises, iron takes the hammer strangely well. Don't ask me why.
tables.TALK.borin.bloodmoon.re.0.t: Want me to stay with you?
tables.TALK.borin.bloodmoon.re.0.s: …Sit by the forge. You don't have to say anything.
tables.TALK.borin.sandstorm.say.0: On sandstorm days I can't open the forge. It's not ash that gets in — it's sand.
tables.TALK.borin.sandstorm.say.1: Sand's caught in the joints of your armor. Leave it and it'll grind away from the inside.
tables.TALK.borin.sandstorm.re.0.t: Knock the sand out for me.
tables.TALK.borin.sandstorm.re.0.s: Have to pry the joints open to knock it out. Sit down, it'll take a while.
tables.TALK.borin.dawn.say.0: Here already, at this hour? The forge hasn't even warmed up.
tables.TALK.borin.dawn.say.1: Iron's soft at dawn. Give it a moment.
tables.TALK.borin.dawn.re.0.s: Then work the bellows. No one waits for free.
tables.TALK.borin.rain.say.0: Quenching goes well on rainy days. The water does the cooling for you.
tables.TALK.borin.rain.say.1: Don't stand by the forge soaking wet. The steam'll hurt your eyes.
tables.TALK.borin.rain.re.0.s: Nails. Nobody buys them, but I keep making them. Hands get restless.
tables.TALK.borin.chdone.say.0: More marks on your weapon. Good marks.
tables.TALK.borin.chdone.say.1: When you come back having finished something, the forge sounds different. Probably my imagination.
tables.TALK.borin.chdone.re.0.t: Take a look at my weapon.
tables.TALK.borin.chdone.re.0.s: The edge has dulled. Leave it; I'll have it honed by morning.
tables.TALK.borin.broke.say.0: No credit. …Is what I'd like to say, but with a face like that, what can I do.
tables.TALK.borin.broke.say.1: No money? Then mine some ore. Iron's always more honest than money.
tables.TALK.borin.broke.re.0.s: Cheap. Nobody mines, nobody buys. So it can't help but be cheap.
tables.TALK.borin.rich.say.0: Your purse sounds nice. That sound won't last long — I'll be taking it all.
tables.TALK.borin.rich.say.1: Buy armor while you have the money. Weapons you can buy in a pinch.
tables.TALK.borin.rich.re.0.s: The best hasn't been made yet. When you bring me the ore — then.
tables.TALK.borin.night.say.0: I'm the only one who keeps the forge alive this late. Iron's quiet at night.
tables.TALK.borin.night.say.1: If the hammering's too loud, say so. …No, even if you do, I won't stop.
tables.TALK.borin.night.re.0.s: How can I sleep when you're not?
tables.TALK.borin.goal.say.0: Got all your tools? Then it's your turn now.
tables.TALK.borin.goal.say.1: When only one thing is left, that one thing is the heaviest.
tables.TALK.borin.goal.re.0.s: It will. If it isn't, that's on you, not the iron.
tables.TALK.borin.night2.say.0: To think a day would come when I don't have to pick up the hammer at night.
tables.TALK.borin.night2.say.1: I get sleepy at night these days. That's the strangest part.
tables.TALK.borin.night2.re.0.s: You too. …Been a while since I heard that, too.
tables.TALK.borin.day2.say.0: These days I get more orders for doorknobs than weapons. That's a good thing.
tables.TALK.borin.day2.say.1: They say the reforger in Dawnhold is better than me. Thinking of going to see.
tables.TALK.borin.day2.re.0.s: My knees. …No, that's an excuse. I'll think about it.
tables.TALK.borin.day.say.0: Come in. What did you break today?
tables.TALK.borin.day.say.1: Don't throw away hides or bones. There are things you can make from those too.
tables.TALK.borin.day.say.2: The knees aren't what they used to be. That's why you do the walking for me.
tables.TALK.borin.day.re.0.t: What are you making these days?
tables.TALK.borin.day.re.0.s.0: Nails, hinges, doorknobs. For people to live, those come first.
tables.TALK.borin.day.re.0.s.1: Weapons come after. …Though lately the order's been flipped.
tables.TALK.mira.grave.say.0: Something of yours is still out there. Not your things — I mean the shard.
tables.TALK.mira.grave.say.1: Where someone dies, a dream pools for a while. Leave it long and something else dreams that dream.
tables.TALK.mira.grave.re.0.s.0: It's the same thing the shards do. Just on a smaller scale.
tables.TALK.mira.hurt.say.0: The starlight in you is wavering. That gets hurt before your body does.
tables.TALK.mira.hurt.say.1: Lose that much blood and the light leaks out with it. That worries me more.
tables.TALK.mira.hurt.re.0.t: What if all the light leaks out?
tables.TALK.mira.hurt.re.0.s: Then touching a shard would do nothing. Sounds like a good thing, but it isn't.
tables.TALK.mira.bloodmoon.say.0: Tonight's moon isn't a star. It's pretending to be one.
tables.TALK.mira.bloodmoon.say.1: On red nights the shards call to each other louder. I can hear it.
tables.TALK.mira.bloodmoon.re.0.s.0: It isn't words. If I had to put it into words — "I'm here."
tables.TALK.mira.bloodmoon.re.0.s.1: That's always what lonely things say.
tables.TALK.mira.sporebloom.say.0: The vale exhaled. The spores don't reach here, but the smell does.
tables.TALK.mira.sporebloom.say.1: That's not reproduction — it's a dream spreading. Land that keeps a shard close too long gets like that.
tables.TALK.mira.sporebloom.re.0.s: The land forgets its own name. People who stay on it long enough become similar.
tables.TALK.mira.sandstorm.say.0: The sand isn't moving because of the wind. It's because something below is stirring.
tables.TALK.mira.sandstorm.say.1: A shard sleeps beneath the dunes too. Every time it stirs, the desert shifts.
tables.TALK.mira.sandstorm.re.0.t: There's a shard under the desert too?
tables.TALK.mira.sandstorm.re.0.s.1: What's stirring is the place where it used to be.
tables.TALK.mira.rain.say.0: When rain washes the ash down, the land remembers its color for a moment. Just a moment.
tables.TALK.mira.rain.say.1: On days like this, mana is heavy. Spells go off half a beat late, so be careful.
tables.TALK.mira.rain.re.0.t: What if my spell is late?
tables.TALK.mira.rain.re.0.s: Step back by as much as it's late. That's all.
tables.TALK.mira.chdone.say.0: One shard has gone quiet. And the light from your hand just thickened by a layer.
tables.TALK.mira.chdone.say.1: You put it to sleep well. Not killed — put to sleep. Remember the difference.
tables.TALK.mira.chdone.re.0.t: What do you mean, put it to sleep?
tables.TALK.mira.chdone.re.0.s.0: I mean it isn't dead. Which means it could be woken again.
tables.TALK.mira.broke.say.0: You're broke. I don't take money — I take something worse, so it's just as well.
tables.TALK.mira.broke.say.1: You can come empty-handed. What I sell isn't things anyway.
tables.TALK.mira.broke.re.0.s: Your time. While you're sitting here, you can't do anything else.
tables.TALK.mira.night.say.0: At night you can see the stars. You can see the gap where one's missing, too.
tables.TALK.mira.night.say.1: I don't sleep at night. If I sleep, I get pulled into the shards' dreams.
tables.TALK.mira.night.re.0.s.0: Someone else's dreams. That's the scariest part.
tables.TALK.mira.night.re.0.s.1: If it were my own dream, I could just wake up.
tables.TALK.mira.dawn.say.0: Mana is shallowest just before sunrise. Go out now and it'll be quiet.
tables.TALK.mira.dawn.say.1: At dawn even the shards sleep a little. Just this much is our time.
tables.TALK.mira.dawn.re.0.s: Good. Be back before the sun's all the way up.
tables.TALK.mira.goal.say.0: The road has narrowed to one. There's no way back now.
tables.TALK.mira.goal.say.1: The shard is waiting for you. "Waiting" isn't a good word here.
tables.TALK.mira.goal.re.0.s.0: No one has ever been fully ready.
tables.TALK.mira.goal.re.0.s.1: But only those who went came back.
tables.TALK.mira.night2.say.0: There — see the new spot in the sky? That's what we sent up.
tables.TALK.mira.night2.say.1: This is the first time in my life the night hasn't scared me.
tables.TALK.mira.night2.re.0.s: Not yet. But I do lie down to try.
tables.TALK.mira.day2.say.0: The star went back where it belongs. But the light in me hasn't gone out.
tables.TALK.mira.day2.say.1: The shards are quiet. Quiet isn't always good, though.
tables.TALK.mira.day2.re.0.s: Still burning. Let's talk when it's burned out.
tables.TALK.mira.day.say.0: There's starlight coming from inside you. A little fainter today than yesterday.
tables.TALK.mira.day.say.1: The stars are calm today. Days like this are rare.
tables.TALK.mira.day.say.2: I'll answer anything you ask. But don't blame me if you don't like the answer.
tables.TALK.mira.day.re.0.s.0: A little fainter than yesterday. That's not all bad.
tables.TALK.mira.day.re.0.s.1: Burning means diminishing. Finish before it burns out and you'll be fine.
tables.TALK.old.hurt.say.0: Bleeding means the body is still trying to keep what's its own. Not bad.
tables.TALK.old.hurt.re.0.s: Then you're not dead yet. Sit.
tables.TALK.old.bloodmoon.say.0: Don't call that red thing the moon. Give it a name and it keeps coming.
tables.TALK.old.bloodmoon.say.1: Ask nothing tonight. The answers will leak out toward it.
tables.TALK.old.sandstorm.say.0: Sand remembers longer than water. Footprints linger a long while.
tables.TALK.old.sandstorm.say.1: What the wind moves is not sand, but places.
tables.TALK.old.sporebloom.say.0: Not everything that exhales is alive. That just burst.
tables.TALK.old.sporebloom.say.1: I have seen the vale do that twice. Both times in summer.
tables.TALK.old.rain.say.0: It's raining. The land isn't crying; water is simply falling. Don't mistake it.
tables.TALK.old.rain.say.1: Don't stand around wet. When you're old, that's the first thing that gets you.
tables.TALK.old.rain.re.0.s: Yes. Mistake less, and you live longer.
tables.TALK.old.chdone.say.0: You've finished one. …Or so you'll think.
tables.TALK.old.chdone.say.1: Well done. It seems no one here will say it to you, so I will.
tables.TALK.old.chdone.re.0.s: Only one thing is ever over. What that one thing was, you learn later.
tables.TALK.old.night.say.0: When you're old, sleep shrinks. So you end up watching the whole night.
tables.TALK.old.night.say.1: Those who come at this hour usually have something to ask. Ask.
tables.TALK.old.night.re.0.s: The night. The more you look, the more it changes.
tables.TALK.old.goal.say.0: If only one thing is left, don't rush. Rush, and that one thing swallows you.
tables.TALK.old.goal.say.1: Go. This is no place for an old man to hold you back.
tables.TALK.old.goal.re.0.s: Yes. Those words mean you'll return.
tables.TALK.old.night2.say.0: Do you see? That spot is where it belongs.
tables.TALK.old.night2.say.1: There's less to ask now. That's not so bad either.
tables.TALK.old.day2.say.0: So the star went back. …I have seen that twice.
tables.TALK.old.day2.say.1: It's not over. It's only that, this time, our turn has passed.
tables.TALK.old.day2.re.0.s.0: Once was when I was young.
tables.TALK.old.day2.re.0.s.1: Back then, no one managed to send it up.
tables.TALK.old.day.say.0: You've come. What are you curious about today?
tables.TALK.old.day.say.1: Sit. What you hear standing doesn't stay with you.
tables.TALK.old.day.say.2: I won't tell you everything I know. If I did, you wouldn't go.
tables.TALK.old.day.re.0.s: Ask. Whether I answer is for me to decide.
tables.TALK.tamer.grave.say.0: My animals smell you and look west. You left something behind.
tables.TALK.tamer.grave.say.1: Take one along. It'll track the scent to where you left it.
tables.TALK.tamer.grave.re.0.s: If it can't, at least it'll get lost with you. Better than a person.
tables.TALK.tamer.hurt.say.0: Come in that state and the animals know first. They're all hiding in the back now.
tables.TALK.tamer.hurt.say.1: Beasts don't stay near someone who's bleeding. Sorry, I can't fix that.
tables.TALK.tamer.hurt.re.0.s: Yeah. Get cleaned up. The animals won't run off.
tables.TALK.tamer.bloodmoon.say.0: I brought all the eggs inside tonight. When the red moon rises, hatching goes strange.
tables.TALK.tamer.bloodmoon.say.1: The animals have been staring one way for a while now. At that moon.
tables.TALK.tamer.bloodmoon.re.0.s.0: They don't hatch right. They come out having dreamed of something else inside the shell.
tables.TALK.tamer.sandstorm.say.0: When a sandstorm blows, the animals all go into their burrows. Instinct.
tables.TALK.tamer.sandstorm.say.1: Sand keeps falling from your footprints. The animals are busy sniffing it.
tables.TALK.tamer.sandstorm.re.0.t: What can they tell from the smell?
tables.TALK.tamer.sandstorm.re.0.s: Where you've been. More accurately than people.
tables.TALK.tamer.sporebloom.say.0: When there's a spore smell, the animals sneeze. Cute, but not good for them.
tables.TALK.tamer.sporebloom.say.1: I shut all the doors today. Their noses are much more sensitive than ours.
tables.TALK.tamer.sporebloom.re.0.s: It settles in a day or two. It always has.
tables.TALK.tamer.rich.say.0: I brought out good eggs today. You'll see from the price.
tables.TALK.tamer.rich.say.1: I recommend the pricey ones to people with money. It's good for both of us.
tables.TALK.tamer.rich.re.0.s: I was waiting for that. Hang on, I'll bring it out.
tables.TALK.tamer.rain.say.0: The animals sleep well on rainy days. They're all sprawled under the eaves.
tables.TALK.tamer.rain.say.1: Don't touch the eggs with wet hands. Not because they're slippery — the animals hate it.
tables.TALK.tamer.rain.re.0.t: I'll let them sleep and go.
tables.TALK.tamer.rain.re.0.s: Yeah. Just keep your footsteps quiet.
tables.TALK.tamer.chdone.say.0: What did you do out there? The animals are all up and staring. You caught something big.
tables.TALK.tamer.chdone.say.1: You look gentle today. Beasts can tell that best.
tables.TALK.tamer.chdone.re.0.s: It still smells of it. Some smells won't wash off.
tables.TALK.tamer.broke.say.0: No money, no eggs. Petting's free, though.
tables.TALK.tamer.broke.say.1: Credit? I'm fine with it, but the animals say no.
tables.TALK.tamer.broke.re.0.s: Sure. That never wears out, no matter how much you do it.
tables.TALK.tamer.night.say.0: The animals are friendlier at night. Probably because there are so many people during the day.
tables.TALK.tamer.night.say.1: There's one that sleeps under the lamppost. That one's the most expensive.
tables.TALK.tamer.night.re.0.t: Tell me about the sleeping one.
tables.TALK.tamer.night.re.0.s.0: No name yet. Name it and I can't sell it.
tables.TALK.tamer.goal.say.0: The animals keep looking at the door. They know you'll be leaving soon.
tables.TALK.tamer.goal.say.1: Take one with you. Better than going alone.
tables.TALK.tamer.goal.re.0.s: Of course. But come back together, too.
tables.TALK.tamer.day.say.0: The animals are all out today. Must be the good sunshine.
tables.TALK.tamer.day.say.1: Know who settled in this city first? Not people.
tables.TALK.tamer.day.say.2: You don't choose an egg — it chooses you. …Sounds pricier when I say it like that, right?
tables.TALK.tamer.day.re.0.s: If you pay. More if you get attached.
tables.TALK.trainer.grave.say.0: You dropped your gear? That's not a mistake, that's a habit. Fix it.
tables.TALK.trainer.grave.say.1: Going back to where you left it is part of the training. Go.
tables.TALK.trainer.grave.re.0.s: Go. Just don't fall in the same spot twice.
tables.TALK.trainer.hurt.say.0: Don't stand in front of me like that. There's nothing to teach you but staying alive.
tables.TALK.trainer.hurt.say.1: You didn't get hit — you failed to dodge. Sit and catch your breath first.
tables.TALK.trainer.hurt.re.0.s.0: Don't move first. Let your opponent commit, then move.
tables.TALK.trainer.hurt.re.0.s.1: That's all there is. The body learns the rest.
tables.TALK.trainer.bloodmoon.say.0: A red night. No training today. I'll be standing on the ramparts.
tables.TALK.trainer.bloodmoon.say.1: It's not the one who goes out on nights like this who's strong — it's the one who counts them.
tables.TALK.trainer.sandstorm.say.0: Practice keeping your eyes open in a sandstorm. That situation will come someday.
tables.TALK.trainer.sandstorm.say.1: Today's training is in the courtyard. Outside, I can't see your stance.
tables.TALK.trainer.sandstorm.re.0.s: What you learn in tight spaces works in open ones. Not the other way around.
tables.TALK.trainer.sporebloom.say.0: Breathe shallow, and long. That's all you'll learn today.
tables.TALK.trainer.sporebloom.say.1: Don't run on spore days. Running makes you breathe in more.
tables.TALK.trainer.sporebloom.re.0.t: Then how do I run away?
tables.TALK.trainer.sporebloom.re.0.s: First, don't get into anything you'd need to run from.
tables.TALK.trainer.rain.say.0: Rainy days are the best for training. When your footing is slick, your stance turns honest.
tables.TALK.trainer.rain.say.1: Learn to grip a weapon with wet hands today. That situation will come someday.
tables.TALK.trainer.rain.re.0.t: How do I grip with wet hands?
tables.TALK.trainer.rain.re.0.s.0: Don't grip harder. That makes it slipperier.
tables.TALK.trainer.rain.re.0.s.1: Brace with your wrist. The fingers only help.
tables.TALK.trainer.chdone.say.0: Your face has changed. You've gotten over something.
tables.TALK.trainer.chdone.say.1: Winning doesn't improve your stance. Come back tomorrow.
tables.TALK.trainer.chdone.re.0.s: Three have kept that promise so far. Try to be the fourth.
tables.TALK.trainer.broke.say.0: No money for training? Pay with your body. There happens to be cargo to move.
tables.TALK.trainer.broke.say.1: Having no money doesn't make you weak. Not putting in the work does.
tables.TALK.trainer.broke.re.0.s: Over there. Move it all and I'll give you one session free.
tables.TALK.trainer.rich.say.0: A heavy purse makes slow feet. Let's fix that first today.
tables.TALK.trainer.rich.say.1: Money only buys you this far. After that, you have to put in the work.
tables.TALK.trainer.rich.re.0.s: The price is fixed. Paying more won't get you more teaching.
tables.TALK.trainer.night.say.0: Coming at this hour means there's something you couldn't do during the day. Good.
tables.TALK.trainer.night.say.1: Night training is half price. But be ready to fall twice as often.
tables.TALK.trainer.night.re.0.s: Good. But keep quiet. There are people at the inn.
tables.TALK.trainer.dawn.say.0: Those who come at dawn last long. That's statistics.
tables.TALK.trainer.dawn.say.1: Warm up before sunrise. The first strike is always the slowest.
tables.TALK.trainer.dawn.re.0.t: Why is the first strike slow?
tables.TALK.trainer.dawn.re.0.s: Because the body is still in yesterday. Ten swings and it arrives in today.
tables.TALK.trainer.goal.say.0: If only one thing is left, today it's sleep, not training.
tables.TALK.trainer.goal.say.1: Your body's ready. Now empty your head.
tables.TALK.trainer.goal.re.0.s.0: Survive the first ten seconds. After that, your opponent makes a mistake.
tables.TALK.trainer.day.say.0: If you've come, loosen up first. Talk comes after.
tables.TALK.trainer.day.say.1: I can rework your stats. But you have to know why you built them that way.
tables.TALK.trainer.day.say.2: I don't make people strong. I just make them not die.
tables.TALK.trainer.day.re.0.s.0: How to fall. That comes first.
tables.TALK.trainer.day.re.0.s.1: How to get up is second. Most people figure that out on their own.
tables.TALK.haran.grave.say.0: Heard you went down somewhere. Rumors travel fastest at the inn.
tables.TALK.haran.grave.say.1: If you left something behind, have a drink first. Nobody goes back to that spot sober.
tables.TALK.haran.grave.re.0.s: Then at least a room. …No, fine, I get it. Be careful out there.
tables.TALK.haran.hurt.say.0: Don't climb the stairs like that. I've kept a room free on the first floor.
tables.TALK.haran.hurt.say.1: Blood won't wash out of the sheets. Stay anyway. I'll deal with the sheets.
tables.TALK.haran.hurt.re.0.t: I can't pay for the room.
tables.TALK.haran.hurt.re.0.s: Today I'll call it paid. But next time I'm charging double.
tables.TALK.haran.bloodmoon.say.0: More guests on red-moon nights. Nobody wants to go out.
tables.TALK.haran.bloodmoon.say.1: I'm closing early tonight. But if you knock late, I'll still open up.
tables.TALK.haran.bloodmoon.re.0.t: Can you leave the door open?
tables.TALK.haran.sandstorm.say.0: Sand gets in through the window frames. I've been sweeping all day.
tables.TALK.haran.sandstorm.say.1: Can't sell drinks with sand in them. Today I'm only serving what's got a lid on it.
tables.TALK.haran.sandstorm.re.0.s: What inn hands its guests a broom? …Thanks, though.
tables.TALK.haran.sporebloom.say.0: I shut the doors. If that smell seeps into the rooms, the guests won't sleep.
tables.TALK.haran.sporebloom.say.1: On spore days, strangely, everyone sits a long time. And talks less.
tables.TALK.haran.sporebloom.re.0.s: They say that smell brings back old memories. Same for me.
tables.TALK.haran.rain.say.0: Today's when laying tiles on the roof pays off. Sounds nice, doesn't it?
tables.TALK.haran.rain.say.1: Drinks sell well on rainy days. Not because people are sad — there's nowhere to go.
tables.TALK.haran.rain.re.0.s.1: If you head out drunk, I'm the one who gets blamed.
tables.TALK.haran.chdone.say.0: From your face, there's something to celebrate today. First drink's on me.
tables.TALK.haran.chdone.say.1: People coming back from something big walk differently. That's how I know.
tables.TALK.haran.chdone.re.0.s: Don't mention it. You coming back alive is my business.
tables.TALK.haran.broke.say.0: I know how your purse is. Water's on the house today, at least.
tables.TALK.haran.broke.say.1: Broke guests stay the longest. That's why I like them.
tables.TALK.haran.broke.re.0.s: …Guests who say that weigh on me the most.
tables.TALK.haran.rich.say.0: Today you get a good room. And I'll charge a good price.
tables.TALK.haran.rich.say.1: I hear gold jingling. You're the only one in this city who makes that sound.
tables.TALK.haran.rich.re.0.s: Third floor. The window faces east. You can watch the sunrise.
tables.TALK.haran.night.say.0: At this hour, only you and I are awake. Always the case.
tables.TALK.haran.night.say.1: Stay the night. I'll make sure nothing happens till morning.
tables.TALK.haran.night.re.0.s: Last one. I say that every time, though.
tables.TALK.haran.dawn.say.1: Watch the sunrise before you go. That's the one thing in this city worth seeing.
tables.TALK.haran.dawn.re.0.s: Then at least take some water. That one's free.
tables.TALK.haran.goal.say.0: No charge for the room tonight. Just get some sleep.
tables.TALK.haran.goal.say.1: One last thing left, I hear. Then eat something before you go.
tables.TALK.haran.goal.re.0.t: I'll eat when I get back.
tables.TALK.haran.goal.re.0.s: Keep that promise. I'm counting those.
tables.TALK.haran.day.say.0: Welcome. Is it a drink today, or a night?
tables.TALK.haran.day.say.1: Someday all these rooms will be full. I won't close up until that day.
tables.TALK.haran.day.say.2: I'm thinking of putting up a new sign, but I don't know what to write.
tables.TALK.haran.day.re.0.s.0: Go ahead. …No, never mind. I have a feeling you'd name it something weird.
tables.TALK.seira.grave.say.0: You dropped something I forged? …That's not about odds, that's about attitude.
tables.TALK.seira.grave.say.1: Go pick it up. I don't want to remake what I've already made.
tables.TALK.seira.grave.re.0.s: Nothing to apologize to me for. It's your gear.
tables.TALK.seira.hurt.say.0: It's not your gear that's cracked — it's you. That I can't fix.
tables.TALK.seira.hurt.say.1: Reforging in that state, your hands will shake and it'll fail. Yours, not mine.
tables.TALK.seira.hurt.re.0.s: …Just once. If it fails, no charge today.
tables.TALK.seira.bloodmoon.say.0: They say reforging goes well on red nights. It's superstition. …But I'm betting a little more today.
tables.TALK.seira.bloodmoon.say.1: The bellows sound lower tonight. Makes me wonder if the fire knows about that moon too.
tables.TALK.seira.bloodmoon.re.0.s: It is. But even I'm giving it one more spin today.
tables.TALK.seira.sandstorm.say.0: Sand gets in and the molten metal's ruined. No forging today.
tables.TALK.seira.sandstorm.say.1: A handful of sand in the bellows and the whole day's gone. So today's a rest day.
tables.TALK.seira.sandstorm.re.0.s: A day for cleaning the bellows. There are no days off.
tables.TALK.seira.dawn.say.0: The fire I kept alive all night is at its best right now. If you want something forged, now's the time.
tables.TALK.seira.dawn.say.1: The hour before sunrise — that's when my hands are most precise.
tables.TALK.seira.dawn.re.0.s: Then sit. The fire's at its best.
tables.TALK.seira.rain.say.0: Hard to keep the fire going on rainy days. Good for cooling, though.
tables.TALK.seira.rain.say.1: When it's humid, the metal doesn't take well. Don't blame me if it fails today.
tables.TALK.seira.rain.re.0.s: Right. If we do it today, you'll end up blaming me.
tables.TALK.seira.chdone.say.0: You finished something. Then it's time to look at your gear again.
tables.TALK.seira.chdone.say.1: Once you're past one hurdle, gear decides the next. That's my job.
tables.TALK.seira.chdone.re.0.t: What should I fix up first?
tables.TALK.seira.chdone.re.0.s: Getting hit less comes first. Hitting comes after.
tables.TALK.seira.broke.say.0: Coming to reforge with no money is a problem. Luck is something you buy, too.
tables.TALK.seira.broke.say.1: I've never done it for free. Never will.
tables.TALK.seira.broke.re.0.s: Yeah. Bring money. I'm not going anywhere.
tables.TALK.seira.rich.say.0: Oh, you can spin it plenty today. Spin enough and it'll go up eventually.
tables.TALK.seira.rich.say.1: With lots of money, the odds look kind. That's an illusion. Know that before you spend.
tables.TALK.seira.rich.re.0.s.0: Eventually. The problem is when "eventually" is.
tables.TALK.seira.rich.re.0.s.1: I told you up front I don't know that.
tables.TALK.seira.night.say.0: They also say things forged at night turn out better. Statistically, no.
tables.TALK.seira.night.say.1: Thanks to the windmill I keep the fire alive at night. I sleep during the day.
tables.TALK.seira.night.re.0.t: Isn't sleeping during the day tiring?
tables.TALK.seira.night.re.0.s: It is. But nights are quiet, so my hands shake less.
tables.TALK.seira.goal.say.0: It's the last one, you said. Then it's time to look at your gear once more.
tables.TALK.seira.goal.say.1: Fail now and there's no time to reforge. So do it now.
tables.TALK.seira.goal.re.0.s: …Just once. My hands are shaking today too.
tables.TALK.seira.day.say.0: Bring anything? If not, just look around.
tables.TALK.seira.day.say.1: Don't ask if I can raise it. Ask if it could go up.
tables.TALK.seira.day.say.2: My hands are honest. Honest isn't always good, though.
tables.TALK.seira.day.re.0.s.0: It could. It could also go down.
tables.TALK.kade.grave.say.0: Tell me the coordinates where you dropped it. …Kidding. No machine can measure that yet.
tables.TALK.kade.grave.say.1: Build a machine that knows where things are, and this city would get rich.
tables.TALK.kade.grave.re.0.t: I'm not kidding, I need one.
tables.TALK.kade.grave.re.0.s: …I'll try to build it. Don't get your hopes up.
tables.TALK.kade.hurt.say.0: Your footsteps sound off right now. Some joint is out of alignment.
tables.TALK.kade.hurt.say.1: The trouble with human bodies is there's no blueprint. If there were, I'd fix you.
tables.TALK.kade.hurt.re.0.t: If there were a blueprint, you'd fix me?
tables.TALK.kade.hurt.re.0.s: I would. Maybe that's why nobody makes one.
tables.TALK.kade.bloodmoon.say.0: On nights with that moon, the turrets' aim goes off. The red light fools the lenses.
tables.TALK.kade.bloodmoon.say.1: I'm going over the rampart systems one by one today. If you're heading out, use the gate.
tables.TALK.kade.bloodmoon.re.0.s: The lenses need replacing. And you'd have to find one in a ruin.
tables.TALK.kade.sandstorm.say.0: Your clothes are full of sand. The dunes moved wholesale, I hear?
tables.TALK.kade.sandstorm.say.1: Save some of that sand. I've got a use for it — drawing glass.
tables.TALK.kade.sandstorm.re.0.s: Good. Draw lenses from this, and maybe even the red moon won't fool them.
tables.TALK.kade.sporebloom.say.0: When spores settle on the contacts, the current goes funny. It's like something alive sticking to the circuit.
tables.TALK.kade.sporebloom.say.1: I've sealed all the vents today. The city's holding its breath.
tables.TALK.kade.sporebloom.re.0.t: What if you open the vents?
tables.TALK.kade.sporebloom.re.0.s: The spores get in. Then the city would breathe and start coughing.
tables.TALK.kade.rich.say.0: If you've got money, stock up on parts. What's missing in an emergency is the most expensive thing.
tables.TALK.kade.rich.say.1: If you're rich, this city's rich. There's no one else.
tables.TALK.kade.rich.re.0.s: Smart. I'll give you a good price when you sell them back to me later, too.
tables.TALK.kade.dawn.say.0: What I've been wrestling with all night just now worked. You're my first customer.
tables.TALK.kade.dawn.say.1: The voltage is most stable at dawn. No one's using it.
tables.TALK.kade.dawn.re.0.s: Turret aim correction. They won't shoot birds anymore.
tables.TALK.kade.rain.say.0: If water gets into the power lines, we're in trouble. I'm up a ladder all day today.
tables.TALK.kade.rain.say.1: Don't stand near the batteries while soaking wet. I mean it.
tables.TALK.kade.rain.re.0.s: …Thanks. Honestly, that was what scared me most.
tables.TALK.kade.chdone.say.0: You finished something. Your walk says it before your face does.
tables.TALK.kade.chdone.say.1: Every time you finish something, it feels like one more page of this city's blueprint gets filled in.
tables.TALK.kade.chdone.re.0.s.0: The one I'm drawing. Of what this city looks like.
tables.TALK.kade.chdone.re.0.s.1: Finish it, and maybe I'll know who built it.
tables.TALK.kade.broke.say.0: No credit on parts. I keep count of where every single rivet came from.
tables.TALK.kade.broke.say.1: No money? Then bring junk. I'm happier to see that anyway.
tables.TALK.kade.broke.re.0.s: Anything. Especially what you don't use. People are worst at throwing away what they don't use.
tables.TALK.kade.night.say.0: I work better at night. During the day, people talk to me. …Not you.
tables.TALK.kade.night.say.1: At this hour the city's quiet. Then you can hear the sounds inside the walls.
tables.TALK.kade.night.re.0.s: One hand's enough. Hold this right here.
tables.TALK.kade.goal.say.0: If only one thing's left, go stocked up on parts. I've seen plenty of people die saving them.
tables.TALK.kade.goal.say.1: I've loaded the turrets with rivets. Your way out should be clear.
tables.TALK.kade.goal.re.0.s: Save the thanks for when you're back. Taking them early is bad luck.
tables.TALK.kade.day.say.0: Good timing. I was one hand short. …Kidding. Half kidding.
tables.TALK.kade.day.say.1: There's wiring inside the walls. We didn't lay it, and it's still live.
tables.TALK.kade.day.say.2: The ruin patterns and this city's patterns are the same. Down to the stroke order — too much for coincidence.
tables.TALK.kade.day.re.0.s.0: That the wiring inside the walls is still live. And that I don't know where it goes.
tables.TERMINALS.0.lines.1: “Third round of staff reductions complete. Mining efficiency: 400% of manual labor.”
tables.TERMINALS.0.lines.2: “We no longer need to send people below. No one dies.”
tables.TERMINALS.0.lines.3: “We have finally done the right thing.”
tables.TERMINALS.1.lines.1: “The machines don't know how to stop. No one who could teach them to stop is left.”
tables.TERMINALS.1.lines.2: “Three lower floors have already dug in. Even we don't know what they're mining.”
tables.TERMINALS.1.lines.3: “Stop authority has been handed to the Overseer. It is the only one that won't die.”
tables.TERMINALS.2.lines.1: “We didn't build this to stop the star. The star was an excuse.”
tables.TERMINALS.2.lines.2: “We just wanted to stop working with our hands. That wasn't wrong.”
tables.TERMINALS.2.lines.3: “What was wrong was not building a way to stop alongside it. Build that first.”
tables.TERMINALS.3.lines.0: “Expansion approval request — no approver. Auto-approved per regulations.”
tables.TERMINALS.4.lines.0: “I was made first. So I understand every order.”
tables.TERMINALS.4.lines.1: “I understand ‘stop,’ too. That one alone I did not carry out.”
tables.TERMINALS.4.lines.2: “If I stop, no one remains. I watched that happen here.”
tables.TERMINALS.4.lines.3: “You have come again. Does that mean I may stop now?”
tables.VILLAGE.1.d: The Ashfall lifted and people came back. It's still closer to a place of survival.
tables.VILLAGE.1.gain.0: 5 residents · Inn · Vault · Reforging Station · Request Board
tables.VILLAGE.2.d: Roofs put back up, a fence around it, and roads you can see at night.
tables.VILLAGE.2.gain.0: Houses rise to two stories with tiled roofs
tables.VILLAGE.2.gain.1: A fenced plot of empty land appears west of the village, and you receive a hoe, sickle and a set of seeds (tilling is up to you)
tables.VILLAGE.2.gain.2: A windmill goes up on the rooftops, and power lines run out to the fields
tables.VILLAGE.2.gain.3: Torches become lampposts, and windows open in the walls
tables.VILLAGE.3.d: Walls raised with the resolve never to be taken again.
tables.VILLAGE.3.gain.0: Ramparts and battlements rise on both sides of the village
tables.VILLAGE.3.gain.1: Auto turrets are mounted on two watchtowers (just keep them stocked with rivets)
tables.VILLAGE.3.gain.2: Two resident guards protect the village
tables.VILLAGE.3.gain.3: Dogyeong the materials dealer moves in — resident merchants 1 → 2
tables.VILLAGE.3.gain.5: A gate and banners go up
tables.VILLAGE.4.d: Once the walls stood, traders followed. Now more can be bought here.
tables.VILLAGE.4.gain.0: Byeoksan the arms dealer moves in — resident merchants 2 → 3. Offers different weapons, armor and accessories each day
tables.VILLAGE.4.gain.1: The three resident merchants each stock one more slot, and items only available at tier 4 are unlocked
tables.VILLAGE.4.gain.2: An Enhancement Anvil goes up beside the Reforging Station — raises gear stats one tier at a time (up to +10)
tables.VILLAGE.4.gain.3: The fields expand on both sides (west up inside the ramparts, east up to the first house)
tables.VILLAGE_TALK.tamer.1: The animals still don't trust these streets. Can't blame them; neither do I.
tables.VILLAGE_TALK.tamer.2: With lampposts up, I can tend the eggs at night. Before, I just packed up when the sun went down.
tables.VILLAGE_TALK.tamer.3: The sound of the gate closing startles the animals. They'll get used to it in a few days.
tables.VILLAGE_TALK.trainer.1: Plenty of ground, but no people. You can train alone, but it's no fun.
tables.VILLAGE_TALK.trainer.2: With a second floor, I can check stances looking down from upstairs. Much better.
tables.VILLAGE_TALK.trainer.3: Don't let your guard down just because two guards stand at the gate. Walls don't replace people.
tables.VILLAGE_TALK.haran.1: Plenty of rooms. Just no one to fill them.
tables.VILLAGE_TALK.haran.2: Since the tiles went on the roof, more guests come on rainy nights. They like the sound, apparently.
tables.VILLAGE_TALK.haran.3: A fortress, huh. I wondered if I should change the sign, but an inn's still an inn.
tables.VILLAGE_TALK.seira.1: The bellows are worn out. Still, it's something that they turn at all.
tables.VILLAGE_TALK.seira.2: Thanks to the windmill I keep the fire going at night. The power lines reach all the way here.
tables.VILLAGE_TALK.seira.3: I forged so many rampart stones building the walls that my hands remember them all now.
tables.VILLAGE_TALK.kade.1: People didn't build this city. Let's shelve that talk for now.
tables.VILLAGE_TALK.kade.2: Seen the fenced plot to the west? The soil's been sorted, but nobody's tilled it. It's waiting for someone with a hoe.
tables.VILLAGE_TALK.kade.3: Two turrets — keep them loaded with rivets and they'll fire on their own. Loading them's your job.
tables.ZONE_CARD.camp.sub: In the Heart of the Ashen Forest
tables.ZONE_CARD.camp.card.line: Where the survivors first lit a fire. From here, we count again.
tables.ZONE_CARD.village.sub: Where People Live Under the Ash
tables.ZONE_CARD.village.card.line: Even after the ash fell, the chimneys still stand. The last street people left behind.
tables.NAME_CALL.elara.1: Come in, {name}. Seeing your face is enough.
tables.NAME_CALL.borin.2: Back again, {name}. What did you break this time?
tables.NAME_CALL.mira.1: Welcome, {name}. The shards are still warm.
tables.NAME_CALL.old.2: {name}. Remembering names is an old man's job.
tables.NAME_CALL.tamer.0: {name}! The little ones spotted you first.
tables.NAME_CALL.tamer.1: Hey, {name}. Want to check the eggs with me?
tables.NAME_CALL.haran.0: {name}! Kept a room free for you.
tables.NAME_CALL.haran.1: Hey, {name}. No time for a drink, I suppose.
tables.NAME_CALL.haran.2: {name}, every rumor today is about you.
tables.NAME_CALL.seira.0: {name}. What are we reforging this time?
tables.NAME_CALL.seira.1: There you are, {name}. Brought your luck?
tables.NAME_CALL.kade.1: Ah, {name}. The machine's making that odd noise again.
tables.NAME_CALL.kade.2: {name}. What parts did you bring today?
tables.ITEMS.watering_can.d: Right-click water to fill it (20 uses), then right-click a plot or crop to water it. A watered plot stays wet for three mornings.
tables.ITEMS.bucket.d: Right-click a water tile to scoop up the whole tile — the water there is gone.
tables.ITEMS.water_bucket.d: Water for a sprinkler. Right-click an empty tile to pour it back as one tile of water.
tables.MACHINE.sprinkler.d: Load water buckets and every morning it waters the nearest plots around it (25 tiles left and right, 6 up and down), up to 500. One bucket covers 50 plots. While it holds water it draws a little power (3) — without power it does not water.
tables.ITEMS.egg_dragon_fire.d: Hot enough to burn your hand. A fire dragon hatches from it.
tables.ITEMS.egg_dragon_earth.d: Heavy as stone. An earth dragon hatches from it.
tables.ITEMS.egg_dragon_storm.d: Your fingertips tingle when you hold it. A lightning dragon hatches from it.
tables.ITEMS.egg_dragon_dark.d: So dark it seems to eat the light. A dark dragon hatches from it.
tables.ITEMS.dragon_treat_1.d: A hatchling must eat this to become a young dragon (at level 9 with full experience).
tables.ITEMS.dragon_treat_2.d: A young dragon must eat this to become an adult (at level 19 with full experience).
tables.ITEMS.dragon_treat_3.d: An adult dragon must eat this to become an elder (at level 29 with full experience).
tables.ITEMS.pet_dragon_fire.d: It melted its own eggshell to get out. Its breath grows longer as it grows.
tables.PETS.dragon_fire.d: It melted its own eggshell to get out. Its breath grows longer as it grows.
tables.ITEMS.pet_dragon_earth.d: The scales on its back overlap like rock. It never hurries.
tables.PETS.dragon_earth.d: The scales on its back overlap like rock. It never hurries.
tables.ITEMS.pet_dragon_storm.d: Sparks fly from its wingtips whenever it shakes its wings.
tables.PETS.dragon_storm.d: Sparks fly from its wingtips whenever it shakes its wings.
tables.ITEMS.pet_dragon_dark.d: Even in shadow, its eyes shine clearly.
tables.PETS.dragon_dark.d: Even in shadow, its eyes shine clearly.
tables.CAVE_TYPES.5.line: Your breath hangs white. The icicles on the ceiling could fall at any moment.
